translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 141

sentences.zh: 【齊紀七】 起強圉赤奮若，盡著雍攝提格，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records 7] From Qiangyu Chifenruo through Zhuoyong Shetige; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records 7] From Qiangyu Chifenruo through Zhuoyong Shetige—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝下建武四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Jianwu year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi, Jianwu year 4 (

sentences.zh: 丁丑，公元四九七年）

translations.literal: dingchou, 497 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingchou, 497 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏立皇子恪為太子。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Wei established Prince Ke as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Northern Wei established Prince Ke as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 魏主宴於清徽堂，語及太子恂，李沖謝曰：「臣忝師傅，不能輔導。」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor feasted at the Qingwei Hall; when the talk turned to the former crown prince Xun, Li Chong apologized, saying, "Your servant was honored to serve as tutor yet could not guide him properly."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Qingwei Hall, when the conversation turned to the deposed crown prince Xun, Li Chong apologized: "Your servant was honored to serve as his tutor yet could not guide him properly."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕尚不能化其惡，師傅何謝也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I myself could not reform his wickedness—why should the tutor apologize!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I myself could not reform his wickedness—why should the tutor apologize!"

sentences.zh: 乙巳，魏主北巡。

translations.literal: On yisi, the Wei emperor made a northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the Wei emperor set out on a northern tour.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書令王晏為世祖所寵任，及上謀廢鬱林王，晏即欣然推奉。

translations.literal: Initially, Minister of Works Wang Yan had been favored and trusted by Emperor Wu; when the present emperor plotted to depose Emperor Yulin, Wang Yan at once gladly supported and advanced him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Minister of Works Wang Yan had been favored and trusted by Emperor Wu of Qi; when the present emperor plotted to depose Emperor Yulin, Wang Yan gladly supported him at once.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王已廢，上與晏宴於東府，語及時事，晏抵掌曰：「公常言晏怯，今定何如？」

translations.literal: After Emperor Yulin was deposed, the emperor banqueted with Wang Yan at the Eastern Mansion; when they spoke of current affairs, Wang Yan slapped his palm and said, "Your Lordship always said Wang Yan was timid—how about now?"
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yulin was deposed, the emperor banqueted with Wang Yan at the Eastern Mansion; discussing current affairs, Wang Yan slapped his palms and said, "Your Lordship always called me timid—what do you think now?"

sentences.zh: 上即位，晏自謂佐命新朝，常非薄世祖故事。

translations.literal: After the emperor took the throne, Wang Yan regarded himself as one who had assisted in establishing the new dynasty and often disparaged precedents from Emperor Wu's reign.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took the throne, Wang Yan saw himself as a founder of the new dynasty and often belittled the ways of Emperor Wu's reign.

sentences.zh: 既居朝端，事多專決，內外要職，並用所親，每與上爭用人。

translations.literal: Having reached the head of the court, he decided many matters on his own; inside and outside, key posts were all filled with his own partisans, and he frequently quarreled with the emperor over appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Once he stood at the head of the government, he decided most affairs on his own, filled important posts at court and in the provinces with his own men, and often disputed the emperor's choice of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上雖以事際須晏，而心惡之。

translations.literal: Although the emperor needed Wang Yan because of the circumstances, he hated him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor still needed Wang Yan for the moment, he loathed him inwardly.

sentences.zh: 嘗料簡世祖中詔，得與晏手敕三百餘紙，皆論國家事，又得晏啟諫世祖以上領選事，以此愈猜薄之。

translations.literal: Once the emperor sorted through the mid-level edicts from Emperor Wu's reign and obtained more than three hundred letters in Wang Yan's own hand, all discussing state affairs; he also obtained Wang Yan's memorial advising Emperor Wu about the present emperor's control of selection—from this his suspicion and dislike grew.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor sorted through Emperor Wu's mid-level edicts and found more than three hundred letters in Wang Yan's own hand on state affairs; he also found Wang Yan's memorial urging Emperor Wu to curb the present emperor's control of appointments—and from this his suspicion deepened.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光勸上誅晏，上曰：「晏於我有功，且未有罪。」

translations.literal: Prince of Shian Yaoguang urged the emperor to execute Wang Yan. The emperor said, "Wang Yan has merit toward me, and he has not yet committed a crime."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shian Xiao Yaoguang urged the emperor to execute Wang Yan. The emperor said, "Wang Yan has served me well, and he has committed no crime yet."

sentences.zh: 遙光曰：「晏尚不能為武帝，安能為陛下乎！」

translations.literal: Yaoguang said, "If Wang Yan could not be loyal to Emperor Wu, how could he be loyal to Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang said, "If Wang Yan could not be loyal to Emperor Wu, how could he be loyal to you!"

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 上遣心腹左右陳世范等出塗巷，采聽異言。

translations.literal: The emperor sent trusted aides such as Chen Shifan out into the streets and alleys to listen for irregular talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent trusted aides such as Chen Shifan into the streets and alleys to gather rumors.

sentences.zh: 晏輕淺無防，意望開府，數呼相工自視，雲當大貴；

translations.literal: Wang Yan was frivolous and unprepared; he coveted the rank of Grand Commander, repeatedly summoned diviners to read his fate, saying he was destined for great honor;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was careless and unguarded; he coveted the rank of Grand Commander, repeatedly called in diviners to read his fate, and said he was destined for great honor;

sentences.zh: 與賓客語，好屏人清閒。

translations.literal: in speaking with guests he liked to send others away for quiet privacy.
translations.idiomatic: when he spoke with guests he liked to dismiss attendants for a private talk.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，疑晏欲反，遂有誅晏之意。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he suspected Wang Yan intended rebellion and formed the intent to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he suspected Wang Yan of plotting rebellion and resolved to kill him.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請鮮于文粲密探上旨，告晏有異志。

translations.literal: Court gentleman Xianyu Wencan secretly probed the emperor's intentions and reported that Wang Yan had rebellious designs.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentleman Xianyu Wencan secretly sounded out the emperor's mind and reported that Wang Yan harbored disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 世范又啟上云：「晏謀因四年南郊，與世祖故主帥於道中竊發。」

translations.literal: Shifan also reported to the emperor, "Wang Yan plans to use the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year to launch a surprise attack on the road with the former commanders-in-chief from Emperor Wu's reign."
translations.idiomatic: Shifan also reported: "Wang Yan plans to use the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year to strike along the road with Emperor Wu's former commanders-in-chief."

sentences.zh: 會虎犯郊壇，上愈懼。

translations.literal: When a tiger entered the suburban altar enclosure, the emperor grew even more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When a tiger entered the suburban altar enclosure, the emperor grew all the more afraid.

sentences.zh: 未郊一日，有敕停行，先報晏及徐孝嗣。

translations.literal: One day before the sacrifice, an edict halted the journey; it was first sent to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaoci.
translations.idiomatic: One day before the sacrifice, an edict halted the procession; it was sent first to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaoci.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣奉旨，而晏陳「郊祀事大，必宜自力。」

translations.literal: Xiaoci obeyed the edict, but Wang Yan stated, "The suburban sacrifice is a great affair and one must certainly exert oneself personally."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci obeyed, but Wang Yan argued, "The suburban sacrifice is a great affair; one must certainly go in person."

sentences.zh: 上益信世范之言。

translations.literal: The emperor trusted Shifan's words all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Shifan's report all the more.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，召晏於華林省，誅之，並北中郎司馬蕭毅、台隊主劉明達，及晏子德元、德和。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Wang Yan was summoned to the Hualin Office and executed, together with Chief of the Northern Gentlemen's Mansion Xiao Yi, garrison commander Liu Mingda, and Wang Yan's sons Deyuan and Dehe.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Wang Yan was summoned to the Hualin Office and executed, together with Chief of the Northern Gentlemen's Mansion Xiao Yi, garrison commander Liu Mingda, and Wang Yan's sons Deyuan and Dehe.

sentences.zh: 下詔云：「晏與毅、明達以河東王鉉識用微弱，謀奉以為主，使守虛器。」

translations.literal: An edict stated, "Wang Yan, together with Yi and Mingda, judged that Prince of Hedong Xuan had weak talent and ability and plotted to install him as ruler, making him guard an empty title."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "Wang Yan, Yi, and Mingda judged Prince of Hedong Xiao Xuan weak in talent and ability and plotted to set him up as ruler, making him hold an empty title."

sentences.zh: 晏弟詡為廣州刺史，上遣南中郎司馬蕭季敞襲殺之。

translations.literal: Wang Yan's younger brother Xu was governor of Guangzhou; the emperor sent Chief of the Southern Gentlemen's Mansion Xiao Jichang to attack and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan's younger brother Xu was governor of Guangzhou; the emperor sent Chief of the Southern Gentlemen's Mansion Xiao Jichang to strike and kill him.

sentences.zh: 季敞，上之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Jichang was the emperor's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang was the emperor's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 蕭毅奢豪，好弓馬，為上所忌，故因事陷之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yi was extravagant and fond of archery and horses—a man the emperor disliked—so he was implicated on this pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi was extravagant and fond of archery and horsemanship—a man the emperor disliked—so he was swept up in the affair.

sentences.zh: 河東王鉉先以少年才弱，故未為上所殺。

translations.literal: Prince of Hedong Xuan had earlier been spared because of his youth and slight talent.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hedong Xuan had earlier been spared because he was young and lacked ability.

sentences.zh: 鉉朝見，常鞠躬俯僂，不敢平行直視。

translations.literal: At court audiences he would bow low and lean forward, not daring to walk level or look straight ahead.
translations.idiomatic: At court he would bow low and stoop, not daring to walk abreast of others or look straight ahead.

sentences.zh: 至是，年稍長，遂坐晏事免官，禁不得與外人交通。

translations.literal: Now, having grown somewhat older, he was removed from office on account of Wang Yan's affair and forbidden to interact with outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he had grown somewhat older, he was removed from office on Wang Yan's account and forbidden to have dealings with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王之將廢也，晏從弟御史中丞思遠謂晏曰：「兄荷世祖厚恩，今一旦贊人如此事；

translations.literal: As Emperor Yulin was about to be deposed, Wang Yan's cousin, imperial censor Wang Siyuan, said to Wang Yan, "Brother, you received great favor from Emperor Wu; now in a single day you have assisted others in such an affair;
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Yulin was about to be deposed, Wang Yan's cousin, imperial censor Wang Siyuan, said to him, "Brother, you owed Emperor Wu a great debt of gratitude; now in a single stroke you have helped others in such a deed;

sentences.zh: 彼或可以權計相須，未知兄將來何以自立！

translations.literal: they may need you for expedients for a time—but do you know how you will establish yourself afterward!
translations.idiomatic: they may need you for a time as an expedient—but how will you stand on your own afterward!

sentences.zh: 若及此引決，猶可保全門戶，不失後名。」

translations.literal: If you take your own life now, you can still preserve your household and not lose your later reputation."
translations.idiomatic: If you take your own life now, you can still preserve your household and your name for posterity."

sentences.zh: 晏曰：「方啖粥，未暇此事。」

translations.literal: Wang Yan said, "I am just eating my porridge; I have no leisure for that matter."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan said, "I am eating my porridge; I have no time for that."

sentences.zh: 及拜驃騎將軍，集會子弟，謂思遠兄思征曰：「隆昌之末，阿戎勸吾自裁；

translations.literal: When he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, he gathered his clansmen and said to Siyuan's elder brother Sizheng, "At the end of the Longchang era, A-Rong urged me to take my own life;
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, he gathered his clansmen and said to Siyuan's elder brother Sizheng, "At the end of the Longchang era, A-Rong urged me to kill myself;

sentences.zh: 若從其語，豈有今日！」

translations.literal: if I had followed his advice, would I have today!"
translations.idiomatic: had I listened to him, would I have what I have today!"

sentences.zh: 思遠遽應曰：「如阿戎所見，今猶未晚也！」

translations.literal: Siyuan immediately replied, "As A-Rong saw it, it is still not too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan at once replied, "As A-Rong saw it then, it is still not too late!"

sentences.zh: 思遠知上外待晏厚而內已疑異，乘間謂晏曰：「時事稍異，兄亦覺不？

translations.literal: Siyuan knew that outwardly the emperor treated Wang Yan generously while inwardly he already suspected him; seizing an occasion he said to Wang Yan, "Affairs are shifting slightly—do you not feel it?
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan knew the emperor treated Wang Yan generously in public while inwardly he already distrusted him; seizing a moment he said, "Affairs are shifting—do you not feel it?

sentences.zh: 凡人多拙於自謀，而巧於謀人。」

translations.literal: Most people are clumsy at plotting for themselves yet clever at plotting against others."
translations.idiomatic: Most people are clumsy at planning for themselves yet clever at plotting against others."

sentences.zh: 晏不應。

translations.literal: Wang Yan did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan made no reply.

sentences.zh: 思遠退，晏方歎曰：「世乃有勸人死者！」

translations.literal: After Siyuan withdrew, Wang Yan finally sighed and said, "There are actually people in the world who urge others to die!"
translations.idiomatic: After Siyuan left, Wang Yan finally sighed and said, "There really are people in this world who urge others to die!"

sentences.zh: 旬日而晏敗。

translations.literal: Within ten days Wang Yan was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Wang Yan was ruined.

sentences.zh: 上聞思遠言，故不之罪，仍遷侍中。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard Siyuan's words, he therefore did not punish him and instead promoted him to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard what Siyuan had said, he did not punish him and instead promoted him to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 晏外弟尉氏阮孝緒亦知晏必敗，晏屢至其門，逃匿不見。

translations.literal: Wang Yan's nephew by marriage, Ruan Xiaoxu of Weishi, also knew Wang Yan was doomed; Wang Yan often came to his door, but he hid and would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan's nephew by marriage, Ruan Xiaoxu of Weishi, also knew Wang Yan was doomed; Wang Yan often came to his door, but Xiaoxu hid and refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 嘗食醬美，問知得於晏家，吐而覆之。

translations.literal: Once he ate a fine sauce and learned it had come from Wang Yan's household; he vomited it out and poured it away.
translations.idiomatic: Once he tasted a fine sauce and learned it had come from Wang Yan's household; he vomited it out and poured it away.

sentences.zh: 乃晏敗，人為之懼，孝緒曰：「親而不黨，何懼之有！」

translations.literal: When Wang Yan fell, people feared for him; Xiaoxu said, "Close kinship without partisan loyalty—what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yan fell, people feared for Xiaoxu; he said, "I was kin but not partisan—what is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 卒免於罪。

translations.literal: In the end he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬戌，魏主至太原。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renxu, the Wei emperor arrived at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renxu, the Wei emperor reached Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以左僕射徐孝嗣為尚書令，征虜將軍蕭季敞為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Left Vice Director Xu Xiaoci was made Minister of Works, and General Who Subdues the Barbarians Xiao Jichang was made governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Left Vice Director Xu Xiaoci was appointed Minister of Works, and General Who Subdues the Barbarians Xiao Jichang was appointed governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，魏主至平城，引見穆泰、陸睿之黨問之，無一人稱枉者；

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Wei emperor reached Pingcheng; he summoned and questioned the faction of Mu Tai and Lu Rui—none claimed to have been wronged;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Wei emperor reached Pingcheng; he summoned and questioned the faction of Mu Tai and Lu Rui—not one claimed innocence;

sentences.zh: 時人皆服任城王澄之明。

translations.literal: at the time people all admired Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: and people at the time all admired Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng's discernment.

sentences.zh: 穆泰及其親黨皆伏誅；

translations.literal: Mu Tai and his confederates were all executed;
translations.idiomatic: Mu Tai and his confederates were all executed;

sentences.zh: 賜陸睿死於獄，宥其妻子，徙遼西為民。

translations.literal: Lu Rui was granted death in prison; his wife and children were spared and exiled to Liaoxi as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rui was granted death in prison; his wife and children were spared and exiled to Liaoxi as commoners.

sentences.zh: 初，魏主遷都，變易舊俗，并州刺史新興公丕皆所不樂；

translations.literal: Initially, when the Wei emperor moved the capital and changed old customs, the new Duke of Xinxing Pi, governor of Bingzhou, was among those who disliked it;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Wei emperor moved the capital and changed old customs, the new Duke of Xinxing Yuan Pi, governor of Bingzhou, was among those who disliked it;

sentences.zh: 帝以其宗室耆舊，亦不之逼，但誘示大理，令其不生同異而已。

translations.literal: the emperor, considering him an elder of the imperial clan, did not press him but only led him with great principle so he would not breed dissent.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor, considering him an elder of the imperial house, did not press him but only guided him with great principle so he would not breed dissent.

sentences.zh: 及朝臣皆變衣冠，朱衣滿坐，而丕獨胡服於其間，晚乃稍加冠帶，而不能修飾容儀，帝亦不強也。

translations.literal: When the court ministers all changed to Chinese robes and gowns and red garments filled the hall, Pi alone wore barbarian dress among them; only late did he gradually add cap and belt, and he could not refine his appearance and bearing—the emperor did not force him either.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ministers all adopted Chinese dress and red robes filled the hall, Pi alone still wore barbarian garb among them; only late did he gradually add cap and belt, and he could not polish his appearance—the emperor did not force him either.

sentences.zh: 太子恂自平城將遷洛陽，元隆與穆泰等密謀留恂，因舉兵斷關，規據陘北。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xun, when about to move from Pingcheng to Luoyang—Yuan Long with Mu Tai and others secretly plotted to detain Xun, raise troops to block the passes, and plan to hold the region north of Xia Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xun was about to move from Pingcheng to Luoyang, Yuan Long with Mu Tai and others secretly plotted to detain him, raise troops to block the passes, and seize the region north of Xia Pass.

sentences.zh: 丕在并州，隆等以其謀告之。

translations.literal: Pi was in Bingzhou; Long and the others reported their plot to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was in Bingzhou; Long and the others reported their plot to him.

sentences.zh: 丕外慮不成，口雖折難，心頗然之。

translations.literal: Outwardly Pi worried it would not succeed; though his mouth argued against it, his heart rather agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Pi feared it would not succeed; though his words argued against it, in his heart he rather agreed.

sentences.zh: 及事覺，丕從帝至平城，帝每推問秦等，常令丕坐觀。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Pi followed the emperor to Pingcheng; whenever the emperor interrogated Tai and the others, he often had Pi sit and watch.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Pi followed the emperor to Pingcheng; whenever the emperor interrogated Tai and the others, he often had Pi sit and watch.

sentences.zh: 有司奏元業、元隆、元超罪當族，丕應從坐。

translations.literal: The officials reported that Yuan Ye, Yuan Long, and Yuan Chao deserved clan extermination; Pi should suffer death by association.
translations.idiomatic: The officials reported that Yuan Ye, Yuan Long, and Yuan Chao deserved clan extermination; Pi should suffer death by association.

sentences.zh: 帝以丕當受詔許以不死，所免死為民，留其後妻、二子，與居於太原，殺隆、超、同產乙升，餘子徙敦煌。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Pi had been granted an edict promising he would not die, commuted death to commoner status, left his second wife and two sons to live with him in Taiyuan, executed Long, Chao, and their younger brother Yisheng of the same mother, and exiled the remaining sons to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding that Pi had been granted an edict promising he would not die, commuted his sentence to commoner status, left his second wife and two sons to live with him in Taiyuan, executed Long, Chao, and their younger brother Yisheng of the same mother, and exiled the remaining sons to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 初，丕、睿與僕射李沖、領軍於烈俱受不死之詔。

translations.literal: Initially Pi, Rui, Vice Director Li Chong, and Commander of the Guards Yu Lie had all received edicts granting immunity from death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pi, Rui, Vice Director Li Chong, and Commander of the Guards Yu Lie had all received edicts granting immunity from death.

sentences.zh: 睿既誅，帝賜沖、烈詔曰：「睿反逆之志，自負幽冥；

translations.literal: After Rui was condemned, the emperor bestowed edicts on Chong and Lie saying, "Rui's rebellious intent relied on the nether world;
translations.idiomatic: After Rui was condemned, the emperor sent edicts to Chong and Lie saying, "Rui's rebellious intent relied on the shades below;

sentences.zh: 違誓在彼，不關朕也。

translations.literal: breaking his oath was on his side—it has nothing to do with Us.
translations.idiomatic: breaking his oath was his own doing—it has nothing to do with Us.

sentences.zh: 反逆既異餘犯，雖欲矜恕，如何可得？

translations.literal: Rebellion differs from other offenses; though We wished to show mercy, how could it be granted?
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion differs from other offenses; though We wished to show mercy, how could it be granted?

sentences.zh: 然猶不忘前言，聽自死別府，免其孥戮。

translations.literal: Yet still not forgetting Our former words, We permit him to die by his own hand in a separate residence and spare his family from execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet still not forgetting Our former words, We permit him to die by his own hand in a separate residence and spare his family from execution.

sentences.zh: 元丕二子、一弟，首為賊端，連坐應死，特恕為民。

translations.literal: Yuan Pi's two sons and one younger brother were foremost as ringleaders of the villains and by association should die; they are specially pardoned as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Pi's two sons and one younger brother were foremost as ringleaders of the plot and by association should die; they are specially pardoned as commoners.

sentences.zh: 朕本期始終而徙自棄絕，違心乖念，一何可悲！

translations.literal: We expected cooperation to the end, yet he cast himself off—heart and words at odds—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: We expected loyalty to the end, yet he cast himself off—heart and words at odds—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 故此別示，想無致怪。

translations.literal: Therefore this separate notice—We trust there will be no taking offense.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore this separate notice—We trust you will not take offense.

sentences.zh: 謀反之外，皎如白日耳。」

translations.literal: Apart from rebellion, the matter is as clear as the noonday sun."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from rebellion, the matter is as clear as noonday."

sentences.zh: 沖、烈皆上表謝。

translations.literal: Chong and Lie both submitted memorials of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Lie both submitted memorials of thanks.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：夫爵祿廢置，殺生予奪，人君所以馭臣之大柄也。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Bestowing and revoking rank and emolument, granting life and taking it—these are the great handles by which a ruler controls his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang says: Bestowing and revoking rank and salary, granting life and taking it—these are the great handles by which a ruler controls his ministers.

sentences.zh: 是故先王之制，雖有親、故、賢、能、功、貴、勤、賓，苟有其罪，不直赦也，必議於槐棘之下，可赦則赦，可宥則宥，可刑則刑，可殺則殺。

translations.literal: Therefore the institutions of the early kings: though there were kin, old associates, the worthy, the able, the meritorious, the noble, the diligent, and honored guests—if guilty, they were not straightaway pardoned; discussion had to take place beneath the pagoda tree and the jujube thorns; if pardonable, pardon; if excusable, excuse; if punishable, punish; if executable, execute.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the institutions of the early kings: though there were kin, old friends, the worthy, the able, the meritorious, the noble, the diligent, and honored guests—if guilty, they were not pardoned outright; the case had to be debated beneath the pagoda tree and the jujube thorns—if pardonable, pardon; if excusable, excuse; if punishable, punish; if executable, execute.

sentences.zh: 輕重視情，寬猛隨時。

translations.literal: Severity and leniency followed circumstance; sternness and mildness followed the times.
translations.idiomatic: Severity and leniency followed the facts; sternness and mildness followed the times.

sentences.zh: 故君得以施恩而不失其威，臣得以免罪而不敢自恃。

translations.literal: Thus the ruler could show favor without losing authority, and ministers could escape guilt without daring self-reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the ruler could show favor without losing his authority, and ministers could escape punishment without daring to rely on privilege.

sentences.zh: 及魏則不然，勳貴之臣，往往豫許之以不死；

translations.literal: With Wei it was not so: meritorious and noble ministers were often beforehand granted exemption from death;
translations.idiomatic: With Wei it was not so: meritorious and noble ministers were often granted immunity from death in advance;

sentences.zh: 使彼驕而觸罪，又從而殺之。

translations.literal: this made them arrogant until they offended, then they were killed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: this made them arrogant until they offended, and then they were killed in turn.

sentences.zh: 是以不信之令誘之使陷於死地也。

translations.literal: Thus an untrustworthy order lured them into the ground of death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus an untrustworthy promise lured them into the ground of death.

sentences.zh: 刑政之失，無此為大焉！

translations.literal: In the failure of penal government, nothing surpasses this!
translations.idiomatic: In the failure of penal government, nothing surpasses this!

sentences.zh: 是時，代鄉舊族，多與泰等連謀，唯於烈一族無所染涉，帝由是益重之。

translations.literal: At this time many of the old clans of Dai were connected with Tai's plot; only Yu Lie's clan was untouched—therefore the emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: At this time many of the old clans of Dai were implicated in Tai's plot; only Yu Lie's clan was untouched—therefore the emperor valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 帝以北方酋長及侍子畏暑，聽秋朝洛陽，春還部落，時人謂之「雁臣」。

translations.literal: The emperor, because northern chieftains and attending sons feared the heat, permitted them to attend court at Luoyang in autumn and return to their tribes in spring—people of the time called them "Wild-Goose ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Because northern chieftains and hostages at court feared the heat, the emperor permitted them to attend at Luoyang in autumn and return to their tribes in spring—people of the time called them "Wild-Goose ministers."

sentences.zh: 三月，己酉，魏主南至離石。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiyou, the Wei emperor went south to Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiyou, the Wei emperor marched south to Lishi.

sentences.zh: 叛胡請降，詔宥之。

translations.literal: Rebellious Hu requested surrender; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious Hu tribes requested surrender; an edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚申，至龍門，遣使祀夏禹。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengshen, he reached Longmen and sent envoys to sacrifice to Yu the Great.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengshen, he reached Longmen and sent envoys to sacrifice to Yu the Great.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，至蒲阪，祀虞舜。

translations.literal: On guihai, he reached Puban and sacrificed to Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, he reached Puban and sacrificed to Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 辛未，至長安。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, he reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 魏太子恂既廢，頗自悔過。

translations.literal: After Crown Prince Xun of Wei was deposed, he greatly repented.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Xun of Wei was deposed, he showed considerable repentance.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉李彪密表恂復與左右謀逆，魏主使中書侍郎邢蠻與咸陽王禧，奉詔繼椒酒詣河陽，賜恂死，斂以粗棺、常服，瘞於河陽。

translations.literal: The imperial censor Li Biao secretly memorialized that Xun was again plotting rebellion with his attendants; the Wei emperor sent Palace Secretaries Xing Luan and Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi with an imperial edict and poisoned wine to Heyang, granted Xun death, buried him in a coarse coffin and ordinary dress at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censor Li Biao secretly reported that Xun was again plotting rebellion with his attendants; the Wei emperor sent Palace Secretary Xing Luan and Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi with an imperial edict and poisoned wine to Heyang, granted Xun death, and buried him in a coarse coffin and ordinary dress at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏大將軍宋明王劉昶卒於彭城，追加九錫，葬以殊禮。

translations.literal: On guimao, Northern Wei Grand General Prince of Songming Liu Chang died at Pengcheng; posthumously granted the nine bestowals; buried with exceptional rites.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Northern Wei Grand General Prince of Songming Liu Chang died at Pengcheng; he was posthumously granted the nine bestowals and buried with exceptional rites.

sentences.zh: 五月，己丑，魏主東還，泛渭入河。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jichou, the Wei emperor returned east, sailing on the Wei River into the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jichou, the Wei emperor returned east, sailing down the Wei River into the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，遣使祀周文王於車，武王於鎬。

translations.literal: On renchen, he sent envoys to sacrifice to King Wen of Zhou at Feng and King Wu at Hao.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, he sent envoys to sacrifice to King Wen of Zhou at Feng and King Wu at Hao.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚申，還洛陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengshen, he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengshen, he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，魏發冀、定、瀛、相、濟五州兵馬二十萬，將入寇。

translations.literal: On renxu, Wei mobilized two hundred thousand troops from the five provinces Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, and Ji, intending to invade.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Northern Wei mobilized two hundred thousand troops from Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, and Ji and prepared to invade.

sentences.zh: 魏穆泰之反也，中書監魏郡公穆羆與之通謀，赦後事發，削官爵為民。

translations.literal: When Mu Tai of Wei rebelled, Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat Mu Pi, Duke of Wei Commandery, had conspired with him; after an amnesty the matter came to light, and his office and noble rank were stripped, reducing him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Tai rebelled in Wei, Chief Secretariat Supervisor Mu Pi, Duke of Wei Commandery, had conspired with him; after an amnesty the plot was exposed, and he was stripped of rank and reduced to a commoner.

sentences.zh: 羆弟司空亮以府事付司馬慕容契，上表自劾，魏主優詔不許；

translations.literal: Pi's younger brother Liang, Director of Works, entrusted his department's affairs to Secretary Murong Qi, memorialized to impeach himself, and the Wei emperor responded with a gracious edict refusing permission;
translations.idiomatic: Pi's younger brother, Director of Works Mu Liang, entrusted departmental affairs to Secretary Murong Qi and memorialized to impeach himself; Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen replied with a gracious edict refusing permission;

sentences.zh: 亮固請不已，癸亥，聽亮遜位。

translations.literal: Liang pressed his request without cease; on guihai, Liang was permitted to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: Liang pressed insistently; on guihai, he was allowed to step down from office.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，魏分六師以定行留。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Wei divided the six armies to fix who would march and who would remain.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Northern Wei divided the six armies to determine marching and garrison forces.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午，魏立昭儀馮氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu, Wei installed Lady Feng, Bearer of the Jeweled Canopy, as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu, Northern Wei installed Lady Feng, Bearer of the Jeweled Canopy, as empress.

sentences.zh: 後欲母養太子恪；

translations.literal: The empress wished to nurse and raise the crown prince Ke as her own son;
translations.idiomatic: The empress wished to raise Crown Prince Ke as her own;

sentences.zh: 恪母高氏自代如洛陽，暴卒於共縣。

translations.literal: Ke's mother, Lady Gao, traveling from Dai toward Luoyang, died suddenly at Gong County.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's mother, Lady Gao, traveling from Dai to Luoyang, died suddenly at Gong County.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏以穆亮為征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wei appointed Mu Liang Grand General Who Conquers the North, Champion of the Secretariat with ceremonial equipage equal to the Three Excellencies, and regional inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Northern Wei appointed Mu Liang Grand General Who Conquers the North, Champion of the Secretariat with ceremonial equipage equal to the Three Excellencies, and regional inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙辰，魏詔中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingchen, Wei ordered martial alert throughout court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingchen, Northern Wei ordered martial law throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，魏立皇子愉為京兆王，懌為清河王，懷為廣平王。

translations.literal: On renxu, Wei enfeoffed the princes Yu as Prince of Jingzhao, Yi as Prince of Qinghe, and Huai as Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Northern Wei enfeoffed Prince Yu as Prince of Jingzhao, Prince Yi as Prince of Qinghe, and Prince Huai as Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 追尊景皇所生王氏為恭太后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored the birth mother of the Jing Emperor, Lady Wang, as Respectful Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored the birth mother of the Jing Emperor, Lady Wang, as Respectful Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏講武於華林園；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Wei conducted military exercises in the Hualin Garden;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Northern Wei conducted military exercises in the Hualin Garden;

sentences.zh: 庚辰，軍發洛陽。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the army set out from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the army set out from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 使吏部尚書任城王澄居守；

translations.literal: He ordered Minister of Personnel, Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng, to remain and guard the capital;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Minister of Personnel, Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng, to remain as guardian of the capital;

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞李彪兼度支尚書，與僕射李沖參治留台事。

translations.literal: He made Censor-in-Chief Li Biao concurrently Director of the Department of Revenue and, together with Vice Director Li Chong, jointly administer affairs of the rear capital.
translations.idiomatic: He made Censor-in-Chief Li Biao concurrently Director of the Department of Revenue and, with Vice Director Li Chong, jointly administer affairs of the rear capital.

sentences.zh: 假彭城王勰中軍大將軍，勰辭曰：「親疏並用，古之道也。

translations.literal: He provisionally appointed Prince of Pengcheng Xie as General of the Central Army and said, "Using both kin and outsiders is the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: He provisionally appointed Prince of Pengcheng Xie as General of the Central Army. Xie declined, saying, "Using both kin and outsiders is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 臣獨何人。

translations.literal: What sort of man am I.
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man am I.

sentences.zh: 頻煩寵授！

translations.literal: to receive favor after favor!
translations.idiomatic: to receive favor after favor!

sentences.zh: 昔陳思求而不允，愚臣不請而得，何否泰之相遠也！」

translations.literal: In old times Cao Zhi sought office and was refused; a foolish subject did not ask yet obtained it—how far apart are fortune and misfortune!"
translations.idiomatic: In old times Cao Zhi sought office and was refused; a foolish subject did not ask yet obtained it—how far apart are fortune and misfortune!"

sentences.zh: 魏主大笑，執勰手曰：「二曹以才名相忌，吾與汝以道德相親。」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor laughed greatly, took Xie by the hand, and said, "The two Caos were jealous of each other for talent; you and I are kin by virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen laughed heartily, took Xie by the hand, and said, "The two Caos were jealous of each other for talent; you and I are kin by virtue."

sentences.zh: 上遣軍主、直閣將軍胡松助北襄城太守成公期戍赭陽，軍主鮑舉助西汝南、北義陽二郡太守黃瑤起戍舞陰。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Army Commander and Direct Attendant General Hu Song to assist the northern defender of Xiangcheng, Cheng Gongqi, in garrisoning Zheyang, and Army Commander Bao Ju to assist the defender of western Runan and northern Yiyang, Huang Yaoqi, in garrisoning Wuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi sent Army Commander and Direct Attendant General Hu Song to assist the northern defender of Xiangcheng, Cheng Gongqi, in garrisoning Zheyang, and Army Commander Bao Ju to assist the defender of western Runan and northern Yiyang, Huang Yaoqi, in garrisoning Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 魏以氐帥楊靈珍為南梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei appointed the Di chieftain Yang Lingzhen regional inspector of southern Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei appointed the Di chieftain Yang Lingzhen regional inspector of southern Liang.

sentences.zh: 靈珍舉州來降，送其母及子於南鄭以為質，遣其弟婆羅阿卜珍將步騎萬餘襲魏武興王楊集始，殺其二弟集同、集眾；

translations.literal: Lingzhen surrendered the province; he sent his mother and son to Nanzheng as hostages and dispatched his younger brother Poluo A-bozhen with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Wei Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi, killing his two younger brothers Jitong and Jizhong;
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen surrendered the province; he sent his mother and son to Nanzheng as hostages and dispatched his younger brother Poluo A-bozhen with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Wei Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi, killing his two younger brothers Jitong and Jizhong;

sentences.zh: 集始窘急，請降。

translations.literal: Jishi, in dire straits, requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi, in dire straits, requested surrender.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁酉，魏主以河南尹李崇為都督隴右諸軍事，將兵數萬討之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingyou, the Wei emperor appointed Henan Intendant Li Chong commander of all military affairs west of Long and led several tens of thousands of troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingyou, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen appointed Henan Intendant Li Chong commander of all military affairs west of Long and led several tens of thousands of troops against him.

sentences.zh: 初，魏遷洛陽，荊州刺史薛真度勸魏主先取樊、鄧。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei moved the capital to Luoyang, Jing regional inspector Xue Zhendu had urged the Wei emperor to take Fan and Deng first.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Northern Wei moved the capital to Luoyang, Jing regional inspector Xue Zhendu had urged Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen to take Fan and Deng first.

sentences.zh: 真度引兵寇南陽，太守房伯玉擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhendu led troops to raid Nanyang; the defender Fang Boyu defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu led troops to raid Nanyang; the defender Fang Boyu defeated him.

sentences.zh: 魏主怒，以南陽小郡，志必滅之，遂引兵向襄陽；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was enraged; because Nanyang was a small commandery, he resolved that it must be destroyed, and therefore led his army toward Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen was enraged; because Nanyang was a small commandery, he resolved that it must be destroyed, and led his army toward Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰等三十六軍前後相繼，眾號百萬，吹脣沸地。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie and thirty-six other armies followed one after another; the host was said to number a million, and their war cries shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie and thirty-six other armies followed in succession; the host was said to number a million, and their war cries shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，魏主留諸將攻赭陽，自引兵南下；

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Wei emperor left the generals to attack Zheyang and himself led troops south;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen left the generals to attack Zheyang and himself led troops south;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，至宛，夜襲其郛，克之。

translations.literal: On guimao, he reached Wan and by night raided its outer wall and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, he reached Wan and by night raided its outer wall and took it.

sentences.zh: 房伯玉嬰內城拒守。

translations.literal: Fang Boyu shut himself in the inner city to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Boyu shut himself in the inner city to resist.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣中書舍人孫延景謂伯玉曰：「我今蕩壹六合，非如向時冬來春去。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Palace Secretary Sun Yanjing to say to Boyu, "I now pacify all within the four seas; this is not like the old days when armies came in winter and left in spring.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen sent Palace Secretary Sun Yanjing to say to Boyu, "I now pacify all within the four seas; this is not like the old days when armies came in winter and left in spring.

sentences.zh: 不有所克，終不還北。

translations.literal: If I do not achieve something, I will never return north.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not achieve something, I will never return north.

sentences.zh: 卿此城當我六龍之首，無容不先攻取；

translations.literal: Your city will be at the head of my six dragons; it must be taken first;
translations.idiomatic: Your city will be at the head of my six dragons; it must be taken first;

sentences.zh: 遠期一年，近止一月。

translations.literal: at the farthest, a year; at the nearest, a month.
translations.idiomatic: at the farthest, a year; at the nearest, a month.

sentences.zh: 封侯、梟首，事在俯仰，宜善圖之！

translations.literal: Enfeoffment and exposure of your head depend on a single glance—plan wisely!
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment and exposure of your head depend on a single glance—plan wisely!

sentences.zh: 且卿有三罪，今令卿知：卿先事武帝，蒙殊常之寵，不能建忠致命而盡節於其仇，罪一也；

translations.literal: Moreover you have three crimes; I now let you know them: you first served Emperor Wu and received extraordinary favor, yet could not establish loyalty and give your life, exhausting your integrity toward his enemy—crime one;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you have three crimes; I now let you know them: you first served Emperor Wu and received extraordinary favor, yet could not establish loyalty and give your life, exhausting your integrity toward his enemy—crime one;

sentences.zh: 頃年薛真度來，卿傷我偏師，罪二也；

translations.literal: in recent years when Xue Zhendu came, you wounded my detached force—crime two;
translations.idiomatic: in recent years when Xue Zhendu came, you wounded my detached force—crime two;

sentences.zh: 今鸞輅親臨，不面縛麾下，罪三也。」

translations.literal: now that the imperial carriage comes in person, you do not bind yourself and come before my standard—crime three."
translations.idiomatic: now that the imperial carriage comes in person, you do not bind yourself and come before my standard—crime three."

sentences.zh: 伯玉遣軍副樂稚柔對曰：「承欲攻圍，期於必克。

translations.literal: Boyu sent his deputy Yue Zhirou to reply, "I hear you intend to invest the city and expect certain capture.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu sent his deputy Yue Zhirou to reply, "I hear you intend to invest the city and expect certain capture.

sentences.zh: 卑微常人，得抗大威，真可謂獲其死所！

translations.literal: A lowly common man who can resist great majesty may truly be said to have found the place to die!
translations.idiomatic: A lowly common man who can resist great majesty may truly be said to have found the place to die!

sentences.zh: 外臣蒙武帝采拔，豈敢忘恩！

translations.literal: As an outer subject I received Emperor Wu's selection and promotion—how could I forget his grace!
translations.idiomatic: As an outer subject I received Emperor Wu's selection and promotion—how could I forget his grace!

sentences.zh: 但嗣君失德，主上光紹大宗，非哺副億兆之深望，抑亦兼武皇之遺赦；

translations.literal: But the successor sovereign lost the Way; our lord has brilliantly continued the great lineage—not only fulfilling the myriad people's deep hopes, but also carrying out the martial emperor's lingering pardon;
translations.idiomatic: But the successor sovereign lost the Way; our lord has brilliantly continued the great lineage—not only fulfilling the myriad people's deep hopes, but also carrying out the martial emperor's lingering pardon;

sentences.zh: 是以區區盡節，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: therefore in my petty person I exhaust my integrity and dare not let it fall.
translations.idiomatic: therefore in my petty person I exhaust my integrity and dare not let it fall.

sentences.zh: 往者北師深入，寇擾邊民，輒厲將士以修職業。

translations.literal: When the northern army went deep before, it harassed the border people; I then encouraged my officers and men to perform their duty.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern army went deep before, it harassed the border people; I then encouraged my officers and men to perform their duty.

sentences.zh: 返己而言，不應垂責。」

translations.literal: Turned back on myself, I ought not to be blamed."
translations.idiomatic: Turned back on myself, I ought not to be blamed."

sentences.zh: 宛城東南隅溝上有橋，魏主引兵過之。

translations.literal: On the moat at the southeast corner of Wan city there was a bridge; the Wei emperor led his troops across it.
translations.idiomatic: On the moat at the southeast corner of Wan city there was a bridge; Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen led his troops across it.

sentences.zh: 伯玉使勇士數人，衣斑衣，戴虎頭帽，伏於竇下，突出擊之，魏主人馬俱驚；

translations.literal: Boyu sent several brave men in spotted garments wearing tiger-head caps to lie in ambush beneath the bridge; they burst out and struck; the Wei emperor's men and horses were all alarmed;
translations.idiomatic: Boyu sent several brave men in spotted garments wearing tiger-head caps to lie in ambush beneath the bridge; they burst out and struck; Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen's men and horses were all alarmed;

sentences.zh: 召善射者原靈度射之，應弦而斃，乃得免。

translations.literal: he summoned skilled archers; Yuan Lingdu shot them and they fell at the twang of the bowstring, and only then did he escape.
translations.idiomatic: he summoned skilled archers; Yuan Lingdu shot them and they fell at the twang of the bowstring, and only then did he escape.

sentences.zh: 李崇槎山分道，出氐不意，表裡襲之；

translations.literal: Li Chong built rafts and divided his forces along the mountains, taking the Di by surprise and striking them from front and rear;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong built rafts and divided his forces along the mountains, taking the Di by surprise and striking them from front and rear;

sentences.zh: 群氐皆棄楊靈珍散歸。

translations.literal: All the Di abandoned Yang Lingzhen and scattered homeward.
translations.idiomatic: All the Di abandoned Yang Lingzhen and scattered homeward.

sentences.zh: 靈珍之眾減太半，崇進據赤土。

translations.literal: Lingzhen's force was reduced by more than half; Chong advanced and occupied Chitu.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen's force was reduced by more than half; Chong advanced and occupied Chitu.

sentences.zh: 靈珍遣從弟建帥五千人屯龍門，自帥精勇一萬屯鷲硤；

translations.literal: Lingzhen sent his younger cousin Jian to lead five thousand men to garrison Longmen while he himself led ten thousand picked warriors to garrison Jiuxia;
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen sent his younger cousin Jian to lead five thousand men to garrison Longmen while he himself led ten thousand picked warriors to garrison Jiuxia;

sentences.zh: 龍門之北數十里中，伐樹塞路；

translations.literal: for several tens of li north of Longmen they felled trees to block the road;
translations.idiomatic: for several tens of li north of Longmen they felled trees to block the road;

sentences.zh: 鷲硤之口，積大木，聚礌石，臨崖下之，以拒魏兵。

translations.literal: at the mouth of Jiuxia they piled great timbers and gathered boulders and rolled them down the cliff to repel the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: at the mouth of Jiuxia they piled great timbers and gathered boulders and rolled them down the cliff to repel the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 崇命統軍慕容拒帥眾五千從它路夜襲龍門，破之。

translations.literal: Chong ordered Commander Murong Ju to lead five thousand men by another route to raid Longmen by night and break it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong ordered Commander Murong Ju to lead five thousand men by another route to raid Longmen by night and break it.

sentences.zh: 崇自攻鷲硤，靈珍連戰敗走；

translations.literal: Chong himself attacked Jiuxia; Lingzhen fought repeatedly and fled in defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Chong himself attacked Jiuxia; Lingzhen fought repeatedly and fled in defeat;

sentences.zh: 俘其妻子，遂克武興。

translations.literal: they captured his wife and children and then took Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: they captured his wife and children and then took Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史陰廣宗、參軍鄭猷等將兵救靈珍；

translations.literal: Liang regional inspector Yin Guangzong and staff officer Zheng You and others led troops to rescue Lingzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Liang regional inspector Yin Guangzong and staff officer Zheng You and others led troops to rescue Lingzhen;

sentences.zh: 崇進擊，大破之，斬楊婆羅阿卜珍，生擒猷等；

translations.literal: Chong advanced to attack and routed them greatly, beheaded Yang Poluo A-bozhen, and captured You and others alive;
translations.idiomatic: Chong advanced to attack and routed them greatly, beheaded Yang Poluo A-bozhen, and captured You and others alive;

sentences.zh: 靈珍奔還漢中。

translations.literal: Lingzhen fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen fled back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞之，喜曰：「使朕無西顧之憂者，李崇也。」

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor heard it, he said with pleasure, "The man who lets me have no worry to the west is Li Chong."
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen heard it, he said with pleasure, "The man who lets me have no worry to the west is Li Chong."

sentences.zh: 以崇為都督梁、秦二州諸軍事、梁州刺史，以安集其地。

translations.literal: He made Chong commander of all military affairs in Liang and Qin and regional inspector of Liang to settle the region.
translations.idiomatic: He made Chong commander of all military affairs in Liang and Qin and regional inspector of Liang to settle the region.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主發南陽，留太尉咸陽王禧等攻之。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Wei emperor set out from Nanyang, leaving Grand Marshal Prince of Xianyang Xi and others to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen set out from Nanyang, leaving Grand Marshal Prince of Xianyang Xi and others to attack it.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏主至新野，新野太守劉思忌拒守。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the Wei emperor reached Xinye; the defender Liu Siji held out against him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen reached Xinye; the defender Liu Siji held out against him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁巳，魏軍攻之，不克，築長圍守之，遣人謂城中曰：「房伯玉已降，汝何為獨取糜碎！」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, the Wei army attacked but could not take it; they built a long encirclement to besiege it and sent someone to say in the city, "Fang Boyu has already surrendered—why do you alone court being ground to bits!"
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, the Wei army attacked but could not take it; they built a long encirclement to besiege it and sent someone to say in the city, "Fang Boyu has already surrendered—why do you alone court being ground to bits!"

sentences.zh: 思忌遣人對曰：「城中兵食猶多，未暇從汝小虜語也！」

translations.literal: Siji sent someone to reply, "The city still has plenty of grain and arms—we have no leisure to heed your petty barbarian talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Siji sent someone to reply, "The city still has plenty of grain and arms—we have no leisure to heed your petty barbarian talk!"

sentences.zh: 魏右軍府長史韓顯宗將別軍屯赭陽，成公期遣胡松引蠻兵攻其營，顯宗力戰破之，斬其裨將高法援。

translations.literal: Wei Right Army Headquarters Chief of Staff Han Xianzong led a detached army to garrison Zheyang; Cheng Gongqi sent Hu Song to lead barbarian troops to attack his camp; Xianzong fought hard and broke them, beheading his lieutenant Gao Fayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Right Army Headquarters Chief of Staff Han Xianzong led a detached army to garrison Zheyang; Cheng Gongqi sent Hu Song to lead barbarian troops to attack his camp; Xianzong fought hard and broke them, beheading his lieutenant Gao Fayuan.

sentences.zh: 顯宗至新野，魏主謂曰：「卿破賊斬將，殊益軍勢。

translations.literal: When Xianzong reached Xinye, the Wei emperor said to him, "You broke the enemy and beheaded a general—this greatly strengthens army morale.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong reached Xinye, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen said to him, "You broke the enemy and beheaded a general—this greatly strengthens army morale.

sentences.zh: 朕方攻堅城，何為不作露布？」

translations.literal: I am now assaulting a strong city—why do you not issue a victory bulletin?"
translations.idiomatic: I am now assaulting a strong city—why do you not issue a victory bulletin?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「頃聞鎮南將軍王肅獲賊二、三人，驢馬數匹，皆為露布；

translations.literal: He replied, "I recently heard that General Who Guards the South Wang Su captured two or three of the enemy and several donkeys and horses, and all were made victory bulletins;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I recently heard that General Who Guards the South Wang Su captured two or three of the enemy and several donkeys and horses, and all were made victory bulletins;

sentences.zh: 臣在東觀，私常哂之。

translations.literal: when I was at the Eastern Observatory I privately often laughed at that.
translations.idiomatic: when I was at the Eastern Observatory I privately often laughed at that.

sentences.zh: 近雖仰憑威靈，得摧丑虜，兵寡力弱，擒斬不多。

translations.literal: Recently, though relying on your majesty's might, I crushed the ugly foe, yet our troops were few and weak and captures and beheadings were not many.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, though relying on your majesty's might, I crushed the ugly foe, yet our troops were few and weak and captures and beheadings were not many.

sentences.zh: 脫復高曳長縑，虛張功烈，尤而效之，其罪彌大。

translations.literal: If I again hung out a long silk banner and falsely inflated my achievements, imitating that fault, the offense would be all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: If I again hung out a long silk banner and falsely inflated my achievements, imitating that fault, the offense would be all the greater.

sentences.zh: 臣所以不敢為之，解上而已。」

translations.literal: That is why I dare not do it and merely report upward to relieve Your Majesty—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dare not do it and merely report upward to relieve Your Majesty—that is all."

sentences.zh: 魏主益賢之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 上詔徐州刺史裴叔業引兵救雍州。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xu regional inspector Pei Shuye to lead troops to rescue Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi ordered Xu regional inspector Pei Shuye to lead troops to rescue Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 叔業啟稱：「北人不樂遠行，唯樂鈔掠。

translations.literal: Shuye memorialized, saying, "Northerners do not like to march far; they only like to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye memorialized, saying, "Northerners do not like to march far; they only like to raid and plunder.

sentences.zh: 若侵虜境，則司、雍之寇自然分矣。」

translations.literal: If we invade their territory, the enemies at Si and Yong will naturally divide themselves."
translations.idiomatic: If we invade their territory, the enemies at Si and Yong will naturally divide themselves."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 叔業引兵攻虹城，獲男女四千餘人。

translations.literal: Shuye led troops to attack Hong city and seized more than four thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye led troops to attack Hong city and seized more than four thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，遣太子中庶子蕭衍、右軍司馬張稷救雍州。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, he dispatched Crown Prince Senior Attendant Xiao Yan and Right Army Major Zhang Ji to rescue Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Emperor Ming of Qi dispatched Crown Prince Senior Attendant Xiao Yan and Right Army Major Zhang Ji to rescue Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲午，前軍將軍韓秀方等十五將降於魏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiawu, Forward Army General Han Xiufang and fifteen other generals surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiawu, Forward Army General Han Xiufang and fifteen other generals surrendered to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，魏敗齊兵於沔北，將軍王伏保等為魏所獲。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Wei defeated Qi troops north of the Han; General Wang Fubao and others were captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Northern Wei defeated Qi troops north of the Han; General Wang Fubao and others were captured by Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以楊靈珍為北秦州刺史、仇池公、武都王。

translations.literal: On bingchen, he appointed Yang Lingzhen regional inspector of northern Qin, Duke of Qiuchi, and Prince of Wudou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Northern Wei appointed Yang Lingzhen regional inspector of northern Qin, Duke of Qiuchi, and Prince of Wudou.

sentences.zh: 新野人張□者帥萬餘家據柵拒魏。

translations.literal: A man of Xinye surnamed Zhang [—] led more than ten thousand households to hold a stockade and resist Wei.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Xinye surnamed Zhang [—] led more than ten thousand households to hold a stockade and resist Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申，魏人攻拔之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, the Wei men attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, the Wei forces attacked and took it.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史曹虎與房伯玉不協，故緩救之，頓軍樊城。

translations.literal: Yong regional inspector Cao Hu was at odds with Fang Boyu and therefore delayed the rescue, halting his army at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong regional inspector Cao Hu was at odds with Fang Boyu and therefore delayed the rescue, halting his army at Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，詔遣度支尚書崔慧景救雍州，假慧景節，帥眾二萬、騎千匹向襄陽，雍州眾軍並受節度。

translations.literal: On dingchou, an edict dispatched Director of the Department of Revenue Cui Huijing to rescue Yong Province, provisionally granting Huijing the tally of authority; he led twenty thousand infantry and a thousand cavalry toward Xiangyang, and all armies of Yong Province were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, an edict dispatched Director of the Department of Revenue Cui Huijing to rescue Yong Province, provisionally granting Huijing the tally of authority; he led twenty thousand infantry and a thousand cavalry toward Xiangyang, and all armies of Yong Province were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主南臨沔水；

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Wei emperor came south to the Han River;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen came south to the Han River;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，還新野。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he returned to Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, he returned to Xinye.

sentences.zh: 將軍王曇紛以萬餘人攻魏南青州黃郭戍，魏戍主崔僧淵破之，舉軍皆沒。

translations.literal: General Wang Tanfen with more than ten thousand men attacked the Wei southern Qingzhou Yellow Outer Garrison; the garrison commander Cui Sengyuan defeated them and the whole army perished.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Tanfen with more than ten thousand men attacked the Wei southern Qingzhou Yellow Outer Garrison; the garrison commander Cui Sengyuan defeated them and the whole army perished.

sentences.zh: 將軍魯康祚、趙公政將兵萬人侵魏太倉口，魏豫州刺史王肅使長史清河傅永將甲士三千擊之。

translations.literal: Generals Lu Kangzuo and Zhao Gongzheng led ten thousand troops to invade the Wei Grand Granary mouth; Wei Yu regional inspector Wang Su ordered Chief of Staff Fu Yong of Qinghe to lead three thousand armored soldiers to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Lu Kangzuo and Zhao Gongzheng led ten thousand troops to invade the Wei Grand Granary mouth; Wei Yu regional inspector Wang Su ordered Chief of Staff Fu Yong of Qinghe to lead three thousand armored soldiers to attack them.

sentences.zh: 康祚等軍於淮南，永軍於淮北，相去十餘里。

translations.literal: Kangzuo and the others were encamped south of the Huai; Yong's army was north of the Huai, separated by more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzuo and the others were encamped south of the Huai; Yong's army was north of the Huai, separated by more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 永曰：「南人好夜斫營，必於渡淮之所置火以記淺處。」

translations.literal: Yong said, "Southerners like to raid camps by night; they are sure to set fires where they cross the Huai to mark the shallows."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Southerners like to raid camps by night; they are sure to set fires where they cross the Huai to mark the shallows."

sentences.zh: 乃夜分兵為二部，伏於營外；

translations.literal: Therefore at midnight he divided his force in two and lay in ambush outside the camp;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at midnight he divided his force in two and lay in ambush outside the camp;

sentences.zh: 又以瓠貯火，密使人過淮南岸，於深處置之，戒曰：「見火起，則亦然之。」

translations.literal: He also stored fire in gourds and secretly sent men across the south bank of the Huai to place them in deep spots, instructing them, "When you see fires rise, do the same."
translations.idiomatic: He also stored fire in gourds and secretly sent men across the south bank of the Huai to place them in deep spots, instructing them, "When you see fires rise, do the same."

sentences.zh: 是夜，康祚等果引兵斫永營；

translations.literal: That night, Kangzuo and the others indeed led troops to raid Yong's camp;
translations.idiomatic: That night, Kangzuo and the others indeed led troops to raid Yong's camp;

sentences.zh: 伏兵夾擊之。

translations.literal: the ambushers struck them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: the ambushers struck them from both sides.

sentences.zh: 康祚等走趣淮水，火既競起，不知所從，溺死及斬首數千級，生擒公政，獲康祚之屍以歸。

translations.literal: Kangzuo and the others fled toward the Huai; fires blazed up everywhere and they did not know which way to go; thousands drowned or were beheaded; Gongzheng was captured alive and Kangzuo's corpse was taken back.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzuo and the others fled toward the Huai; fires blazed up everywhere and they did not know which way to go; thousands drowned or were beheaded; Gongzheng was captured alive and Kangzuo's corpse was taken back.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史裴叔業侵魏楚王戍，肅復令永擊之。

translations.literal: Yu regional inspector Pei Shuye invaded the Wei Prince of Chu's garrison; Su again ordered Yong to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu regional inspector Pei Shuye invaded the Wei Prince of Chu's garrison; Wang Su again ordered Yong to attack him.

sentences.zh: 永將心腹一人馳詣楚王戍，令填外塹，夜伏戰士千人於城外。

translations.literal: Yong took one trusted man and galloped to the Prince of Chu's garrison, ordering the outer moat filled in and a thousand warriors hidden outside the wall by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yong took one trusted man and galloped to the Prince of Chu's garrison, ordered the outer moat filled in, and hid a thousand warriors outside the wall by night.

sentences.zh: 曉而叔業等至城東，部分將置長圍。

translations.literal: At dawn Shuye and the others reached the east of the city and were deploying generals to set a long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Shuye and the others reached the east of the city and were deploying generals to set a long encirclement.

sentences.zh: 永伏兵擊其後軍，破之。

translations.literal: Yong's ambush struck their rear army and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's ambush struck their rear army and broke it.

sentences.zh: 叔業留將佐守營，自將精兵數千救之。

translations.literal: Shuye left his officers and staff to guard the camp and himself led several thousand picked troops to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye left his officers and staff to guard the camp and himself led several thousand picked troops to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 永登門樓，望叔業南行數里，則開門奮擊，大破之，獲叔業傘扇、鼓幕、甲仗萬餘。

translations.literal: Yong mounted the gate tower; when he saw Shuye marching south several li, he opened the gates and struck fiercely, routing them greatly and seizing more than ten thousand of Shuye's parasols, drums, curtains, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yong mounted the gate tower; when he saw Shuye marching south several li, he opened the gates and struck fiercely, routing them greatly and seizing more than ten thousand of Shuye's parasols, drums, curtains, armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 叔業進退失據，遂走。

translations.literal: Shuye lost his footing in advance and retreat and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye lost his footing in advance and retreat and fled.

sentences.zh: 左右欲追之，永曰：「吾弱卒不滿三千，彼精甲猶盛，非力屈而敗，自墜吾計中耳。

translations.literal: Those at his side wished to pursue; Yong said, "My weak troops number fewer than three thousand; their fine armor is still strong—they did not fall from exhaustion but fell into my trap.
translations.idiomatic: Those at his side wished to pursue; Yong said, "My weak troops number fewer than three thousand; their fine armor is still strong—they did not fall from exhaustion but fell into my trap.

sentences.zh: 既不測我之虛實，足使喪膽。

translations.literal: If they cannot gauge my strength and weakness, that is enough to make them lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot gauge my strength and weakness, that is enough to make them lose heart.

sentences.zh: 俘此足矣，何更追之！」

translations.literal: Capturing this much is enough—why pursue further!"
translations.idiomatic: Capturing this much is enough—why pursue further!"

sentences.zh: 魏主遣謁者就拜永安遠將軍、汝南太守，封貝丘縣男。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent an envoy to appoint him on the spot General of Distant Pacification of Yong'an and defender of Runan, enfeoffing him as Baron of Beqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen sent an envoy to appoint him on the spot General of Distant Pacification of Yong'an and defender of Runan, enfeoffing him as Baron of Beqiu.

sentences.zh: 永有勇力，好學能文。

translations.literal: Yong had courage and strength and loved learning and could write.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had courage and strength, loved learning, and could write.

sentences.zh: 魏主常歎曰：「上馬能擊賊，下馬作露版，唯傅修期耳！」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor often sighed and said, "On horseback he can strike the enemy; off horseback he can draft victory bulletins—only Fu Xiuyuan!"
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen often sighed and said, "On horseback he can strike the enemy; off horseback he can draft victory bulletins—only Fu Xiuyuan!"

sentences.zh: 曲江公遙欣好武事，上以諸子尚幼，內親則仗遙欣兄弟，外親則倚後弟西中郎長史彭城劉暄、內弟太子詹事江祏。

translations.literal: Duke of Qujiang Yao Xin loved military affairs; because the emperor's sons were still young, for inner kin he relied on Yao Xin and his brothers, and for outer kin he relied on his empress's younger brother, Chief of Staff of the Western Palace Attendant Liu Xuan of Pengcheng, and his wife's younger brother, Steward of the Crown Prince Jiang Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Qujiang Yao Xin loved military affairs; because Emperor Ming of Qi's sons were still young, for inner kin he relied on Yao Xin and his brothers, and for outer kin he relied on his empress's younger brother, Chief of Staff of the Western Palace Attendant Liu Xuan of Pengcheng, and his wife's younger brother, Steward of the Crown Prince Jiang Shi.

sentences.zh: 故以始安王遙光為揚州刺史，居中用事；

translations.literal: Therefore he made Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang regional inspector of Yang and let him wield power at court;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he made Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang regional inspector of Yang and let him wield power at court;

sentences.zh: 遙欣為都督荊、雍等七州諸軍事、荊州刺史，鎮據西面。

translations.literal: Yao Xin was made commander of all military affairs in Jing, Yong, and six other provinces and regional inspector of Jing, holding the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xin was made commander of all military affairs in Jing, Yong, and six other provinces and regional inspector of Jing, holding the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 而遙欣在江陵，多招才勇，厚自封殖，上甚惡之。

translations.literal: But Yao Xin was at Jiangling, recruiting many men of talent and courage and enriching himself greatly; the emperor hated this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: But Yao Xin was at Jiangling, recruiting many men of talent and courage and enriching himself greatly; Emperor Ming of Qi hated this deeply.

sentences.zh: 遙欣侮南郡太守劉季連，季連密表遙欣有異跡；

translations.literal: Yao Xin insulted the defender of Nan Commandery, Liu Jilian; Jilian secretly memorialized that Yao Xin showed signs of disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xin insulted the defender of Nan Commandery, Liu Jilian; Jilian secretly memorialized that Yao Xin showed signs of disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 上乃以季連為益州刺史，使據遙欣上流以制之。

translations.literal: the emperor therefore made Jilian regional inspector of Yi to hold the upper reaches against Yao Xin.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor therefore made Jilian regional inspector of Yi to hold the upper reaches against Yao Xin.

sentences.zh: 季連，思考之子也。

translations.literal: Jilian was the son of Liu Sikao.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian was the son of Liu Sikao.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高昌王馬儒遣司馬王體玄入貢於魏，請兵迎接，求舉國內徙；

translations.literal: That year, King Ma Ru of Gaochang sent Secretary Wang Tixuan to offer tribute to Wei, requesting troops to escort him and asking to move the whole state inward;
translations.idiomatic: That year, King Ma Ru of Gaochang sent Secretary Wang Tixuan to offer tribute to Northern Wei, requesting troops to escort him and asking to move the whole state inward;

sentences.zh: 魏主遣明威將軍韓安保迎之，割伊吾之地五百里以居儒眾。

translations.literal: the Wei emperor sent General of Illustrious Might Han Wenbao to welcome him and carved out five hundred li of Yiwu territory to settle Ru's people.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen sent General of Illustrious Might Han Wenbao to welcome him and carved out five hundred li of Yiwu territory to settle Ru's people.

sentences.zh: 儒遣左長史顧禮、右長史金城麴嘉將步騎一千五百迎安保，而安保不至；

translations.literal: Ru sent Left Chief of Staff Gu Li and Right Chief of Staff Qu Jia of Jincheng with fifteen hundred infantry and cavalry to welcome Wenbao, but Wenbao did not arrive;
translations.idiomatic: Ru sent Left Chief of Staff Gu Li and Right Chief of Staff Qu Jia of Jincheng with fifteen hundred infantry and cavalry to welcome Wenbao, but Wenbao did not arrive;

sentences.zh: 禮、嘉還高昌，安保亦還伊吾。

translations.literal: Li and Jia returned to Gaochang and Wenbao also returned to Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Jia returned to Gaochang and Wenbao also returned to Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 安保遣其屬朝興安等使高昌，儒復遣顧禮將世子義舒迎安保，至白棘城，去高昌百六十里。

translations.literal: Wenbao sent his subordinate Chao Xing'an and others as envoys to Gaochang; Ru again sent Gu Li to lead the heir Ma Yishu to welcome Wenbao; they reached Baidi City, one hundred sixty li from Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao sent his subordinate Chao Xing'an and others as envoys to Gaochang; Ru again sent Gu Li to lead the heir Ma Yishu to welcome Wenbao; they reached Baidi City, one hundred sixty li from Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 高昌舊人戀土，不願東遷，相與殺儒，立麴喜為王，復臣於柔然。

translations.literal: The old people of Gaochang were attached to their land and unwilling to move east; together they killed Ru, installed Qu Xi as king, and again submitted to Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: The old people of Gaochang were attached to their land and unwilling to move east; together they killed Ru, installed Qu Xi as king, and again submitted to Rouran.

sentences.zh: 安保獨與顧禮、馬義舒還洛陽。

translations.literal: Wenbao alone returned to Luoyang with Gu Li and Ma Yishu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao alone returned to Luoyang with Gu Li and Ma Yishu.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝下永泰元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Yongtai year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi, Yongtai year 1 (

sentences.zh: 戊寅，公元四九八年）

translations.literal: wuyin, 498 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuyin, 498 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸未朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 加中軍將軍徐孝嗣開府儀同三司，孝嗣固辭。

translations.literal: General of the Central Army Xu Xiaosi was promoted to Champion of the Secretariat with ceremonial equipage equal to the Three Excellencies; Xiaosi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Central Army Xu Xiaosi was promoted to Champion of the Secretariat with ceremonial equipage equal to the Three Excellencies; Xiaosi firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 魏軍李佐攻新野，丁亥，拔之，縛劉思忌，問之曰：「今欲降未？」

translations.literal: Wei officer Li Zuo attacked Xinye; on dinghai it was taken; he bound Liu Siji and asked him, "Do you wish to surrender now?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei officer Li Zuo attacked Xinye; on dinghai it was taken; he bound Liu Siji and asked him, "Do you wish to surrender now?"

sentences.zh: 思忌曰：「寧為南鬼，不為北臣！」

translations.literal: Siji said, "I would rather be a ghost of the south than a subject of the north!"
translations.idiomatic: Siji said, "I would rather be a ghost of the south than a subject of the north!"

sentences.zh: 乃殺之。

translations.literal: Then they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Then they killed him.

sentences.zh: 於是沔北大震。

translations.literal: At this the region north of the Han was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: At this the region north of the Han was greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 戊子，湖陽戍主蔡道福，辛卯，赭陽戍主成公期，壬辰，舞陰戍主黃瑤起、南鄉太守席謙，相繼南遁。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the garrison commander of Huyang, Cai Daofu; on xinmao, the garrison commander of Zheyang, Cheng Gongqi; on renchen, the garrison commander of Wuyin, Huang Yaoqi, and the defender of Nanxiang, Xi Qian, fled south in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the garrison commander of Huyang, Cai Daofu; on xinmao, the garrison commander of Zheyang, Cheng Gongqi; on renchen, the garrison commander of Wuyin, Huang Yaoqi, and the defender of Nanxiang, Xi Qian, fled south in succession.

sentences.zh: 瑤起為魏所獲，魏主以賜王肅，肅臠而食之。

translations.literal: Yaoqi was captured by Wei; the Wei emperor gave him to Wang Su, and Su cut off his flesh and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqi was captured by Northern Wei; Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen gave him to Wang Su, and Su cut off his flesh and ate it.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，命太尉陳顯達救雍州。

translations.literal: On yisi, he ordered Grand Marshal Chen Xianda to rescue Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Emperor Ming of Qi ordered Grand Marshal Chen Xianda to rescue Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 上有疾，以近親寡弱，忌高、武子孫。

translations.literal: The emperor was ill; because his close kin were few and weak, he feared the descendants of the Gao and Wu emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi was ill; because his close kin were few and weak, he feared the descendants of the Gao and Wu emperors.

sentences.zh: 時高、武子孫猶有十王，每朔望入朝，上還後宮輒歎息曰：「我及司徒諸子皆不長，高、武子孫日益長大！」

translations.literal: At that time there were still ten princes among the Gao and Wu descendants; on each new and full moon they entered court; after the emperor returned to the inner palace he would sigh and say, "I and the sons of the Director of Works are none of us growing tall, while the Gao and Wu descendants grow taller day by day!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were still ten princes among the Gao and Wu descendants; on each new and full moon they entered court; after the emperor returned to the inner palace he would sigh and say, "I and the sons of the Director of Works are none of us growing tall, while the Gao and Wu descendants grow taller day by day!"

sentences.zh: 上欲盡除高、武之族，以微言問陳顯達，對曰：「此等豈足介慮！」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to exterminate the Gao and Wu clans; he probed Chen Xianda with veiled words, and he replied, "These are hardly worth worrying over!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi wished to exterminate the Gao and Wu clans; he probed Chen Xianda with veiled words, and he replied, "These are hardly worth worrying over!"

sentences.zh: 以問揚州刺史始安王遙光，遙光以為當以次施行。

translations.literal: He asked Yang regional inspector Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang, who thought they should be dealt with step by step.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Yang regional inspector Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang, who thought they should be dealt with step by step.

sentences.zh: 遙光有足疾，上常令乘輿自望賢門入。

translations.literal: Yao Guang had an ailment of the foot; the emperor often had him enter by carriage through the Wangxian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang had an ailment of the foot; the emperor often had him enter by carriage through the Wangxian Gate.

sentences.zh: 每與上屏人久語畢。

translations.literal: Each time he and the emperor spoke at length behind screens until finished.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he and the emperor spoke at length behind screens until finished.

sentences.zh: 上索香火，嗚咽流涕，明日必有所誅。

translations.literal: The emperor would ask for incense, weep and sob, and the next day there would certainly be executions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would ask for incense, weep and sob, and the next day there would certainly be executions.

sentences.zh: 會上疾暴甚，絕而復甦，遙光遂行其策。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness suddenly grew very severe and he stopped breathing then revived, Yao Guang carried out his plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness suddenly grew very severe and he stopped breathing then revived, Yao Guang carried out his plan.

sentences.zh: 丁未，殺河東王鉉、臨賀王子岳、西陽王子文、永陽王子峻、南康王子琳、衡陽王子鈱、湘東王子建、南郡王子夏、桂陽王昭粲、巴陵王昭秀，於是太祖、世祖及世宗諸子皆盡矣。

translations.literal: On dingwei, they killed Prince of Hedong Xuan, Prince of Linhe Ziyue, Prince of Xiyang Ziwen, Prince of Yongyang Zijun, Prince of Nankang Zilin, Prince of Hengyang Ziyin, Prince of Xiangdong Zijian, Prince of Nan Commandery Zixia, Prince of Guiyang Zhao Can, and Prince of Baling Zhao Xiu; thus the sons of the Taizu, Shizu, and Shizong were all gone.
