translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, they killed Prince of Hedong Xuan, Prince of Linhe Ziyue, Prince of Xiyang Ziwen, Prince of Yongyang Zijun, Prince of Nankang Zilin, Prince of Hengyang Ziyin, Prince of Xiangdong Zijian, Prince of Nan Commandery Zixia, Prince of Guiyang Zhao Can, and Prince of Baling Zhao Xiu; thus the sons of Taizu, Shizu, and Shizong were all gone.

sentences.zh: 鉉等已死，乃使公卿奏其罪狀，請誅之，下詔不許；

translations.literal: After Xuan and the others were already dead, they had the high ministers memorialize their crimes and request execution; an edict refused permission;
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan and the others were already dead, they had the high ministers memorialize their crimes and request execution; an edict refused permission;

sentences.zh: 再奏，然後許之。

translations.literal: they memorialized again, and only then was permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: they memorialized again, and only then was permission granted.

sentences.zh: 南康侍讀濟陽江泌哭子琳，淚盡，繼之以血；

translations.literal: Jiang Mi of Jiyang, reader for the Prince of Nankang, wept for Zilin until his tears ran dry and then blood followed;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mi of Jiyang, reader for the Prince of Nankang, wept for Zilin until his tears ran dry and then blood followed;

sentences.zh: 親視殯葬畢，乃去。

translations.literal: he personally oversaw the funeral and burial and only then left.
translations.idiomatic: he personally oversaw the funeral and burial and only then left.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏主如南陽。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Wei emperor went to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen went to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸丑，詔左衛將軍蕭惠休等救壽陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guichou, an edict ordered Left Guard General Xiao Huiyou and others to rescue Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guichou, an edict ordered Left Guard General Xiao Huiyou and others to rescue Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏人拔宛北城，房伯玉面縛出降。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Wei men took the north city of Wan; Fang Boyu bound himself and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Wei forces took the north city of Wan; Fang Boyu bound himself and came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 伯玉從父弟思安為魏中統軍，數為伯玉泣請，魏主乃赦之。

translations.literal: Boyu's cousin from the father's side, Si'an, was a central commander in Wei; he repeatedly pleaded for Boyu in tears, and the Wei emperor then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu's cousin from the father's side, Si'an, was a central commander in Wei; he repeatedly pleaded for Boyu in tears, and Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主如新。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Wei emperor went to Xin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen went to Xin.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以彭城王勰為使持節、都督南征諸軍事、中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Prince of Pengcheng Xie was made bearer of the staff of office, commander of all military affairs of the southern campaign, General of the Central Army, and Champion of the Secretariat with ceremonial equipage equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Prince of Pengcheng Xie was made bearer of the staff of office, commander of all military affairs of the southern campaign, General of the Central Army, and Champion of the Secretariat with ceremonial equipage equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬午朔，崔慧景、蕭衍大敗於鄧城。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renwu, the new moon, Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan were greatly defeated at Deng city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renwu, the new moon, Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan were greatly defeated at Deng city.

sentences.zh: 時慧景至襄陽，五郡已沒，慧景與衍及軍主劉山陽、傅法憲等帥五千餘人進行鄧城，魏數萬騎奄至，諸軍登城拒守。

translations.literal: At that time Huijing had reached Xiangyang; five commanderies had already fallen; Huijing, together with Yan and Army Commanders Liu Shanyang, Fu Faxian, and others led more than five thousand men to advance on Deng city; several tens of thousands of Wei cavalry suddenly arrived and the armies mounted the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huijing had reached Xiangyang; five commanderies had already fallen; Huijing, together with Yan and Army Commanders Liu Shanyang, Fu Faxian, and others led more than five thousand men to advance on Deng city; several tens of thousands of Wei cavalry suddenly arrived and the armies mounted the walls to resist.

sentences.zh: 時將士蓐食輕行，皆有饑懼之色。

translations.literal: At the time the officers and men were traveling light on bedding rations and all had the color of hunger and fear.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the officers and men were traveling light on bedding rations and all had the color of hunger and fear.

sentences.zh: 衍欲出戰，慧景曰：「虜不夜圍人城，待日暮自當去。」

translations.literal: Yan wished to go out and fight; Huijing said, "The barbarians do not invest cities by night; wait until evening and they will naturally leave."
translations.idiomatic: Yan wished to go out and fight; Huijing said, "The barbarians do not invest cities by night; wait until evening and they will naturally leave."

sentences.zh: 既而魏眾轉至。

translations.literal: Before long the Wei host turned and came on.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Wei host turned and came on.

sentences.zh: 慧景於南門拔軍去，諸軍不相知，相繼皆遁。

translations.literal: Huijing at the south gate drew off his army and left; the armies did not know of one another and fled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing at the south gate drew off his army and left; the armies did not know of one another and fled in succession.

sentences.zh: 魏兵自北門入，劉山陽與部曲數百人斷後死戰，且戰且卻行。

translations.literal: Wei troops entered from the north gate; Liu Shanyang and several hundred of his personal followers fought a rear-guard action to the death, fighting as they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops entered from the north gate; Liu Shanyang and several hundred of his personal followers fought a rear-guard action to the death, fighting as they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 慧景過鬧溝，軍人相蹈藉，橋皆斷壞。

translations.literal: Huijing crossed Naogou; soldiers trampled one another and the bridges were all broken.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing crossed Naogou; soldiers trampled one another and the bridges were all broken.

sentences.zh: 魏兵夾路射之，殺傅法憲，士卒赴溝死者相枕，山陽取襖仗填溝乘之，得免。

translations.literal: Wei troops shot them from both sides of the road, killing Fu Faxian; soldiers who plunged into the ditch died piled on one another; Shanyang took padded coats and gear to fill the ditch and cross, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops shot them from both sides of the road, killing Fu Faxian; soldiers who plunged into the ditch died piled on one another; Shanyang took padded coats and gear to fill the ditch and cross, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 魏主將大兵追之，晡時至沔。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was about to pursue with a great army; at the hour of shen he reached the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen was about to pursue with a great army; at the hour of shen he reached the Han.

sentences.zh: 山陽據城苦戰，至暮，魏兵乃退。

translations.literal: Shanyang held the city and fought bitterly; by evening the Wei army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang held the city and fought bitterly; by evening the Wei army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 諸軍恐懼，是夕，皆下船還襄陽。

translations.literal: The armies were terrified; that evening they all went aboard ship and returned to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were terrified; that evening they all went aboard ship and returned to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏主將十萬眾，羽儀華蓋，以圍樊城，曹虎閉門自守。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Wei emperor led a hundred thousand men with feathered banners and ornate canopies to invest Fancheng; Cao Hu shut the gates and held out.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen led a hundred thousand men with feathered banners and ornate canopies to invest Fancheng; Cao Hu shut the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 魏主臨沔水，望襄陽岸，乃去，如湖陽；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor came to the Han River and gazed at the Xiangyang shore, then departed and went to Huyang;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen came to the Han River and gazed at the Xiangyang shore, then departed and went to Huyang;

sentences.zh: 辛亥，如懸瓠。

translations.literal: on xinhai, he went to Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: on xinhai, he went to Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 魏鎮南將軍王肅攻義陽，裴叔業將兵五萬圍渦陽以救義陽。

translations.literal: Wei General Who Guards the South Wang Su attacked Yiyang; Pei Shuye led fifty thousand troops to invest Guoyang to rescue Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei General Who Guards the South Wang Su attacked Yiyang; Pei Shuye led fifty thousand troops to invest Guoyang to rescue Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 魏南兗州刺史濟北孟表守渦陽，糧盡，食草木皮葉。

translations.literal: Wei southern Yan regional inspector Meng Biao of Jibei defended Guoyang; grain was exhausted and they ate plants, tree bark, and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Wei southern Yan regional inspector Meng Biao of Jibei defended Guoyang; grain was exhausted and they ate plants, tree bark, and leaves.

sentences.zh: 叔業積所殺魏人高五丈以示城內；

translations.literal: Shuye piled the Wei dead he had killed to a height of five zhang to show inside the city;
translations.idiomatic: Shuye piled the Wei dead he had killed to a height of five zhang to show inside the city;

sentences.zh: 別遣軍主蕭瑰等攻龍亢，魏廣陵王羽救之。

translations.literal: separately he sent Army Commander Xiao Gui and others to attack Longkang; Wei Prince of Guangling Yu came to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: separately he sent Army Commander Xiao Gui and others to attack Longkang; Wei Prince of Guangling Yu came to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 叔業引兵擊羽，大破之，追獲其節。

translations.literal: Shuye led troops to strike Yu and routed him greatly, pursued and seized his tally of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye led troops to strike Yu and routed him greatly, pursued and seized his tally of authority.

sentences.zh: 魏主使安遠將軍傅永、征虜將軍劉藻、假輔國將軍高聰等救渦陽，並受王肅節度。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent General of Pacifying the Distant Fu Yong, General Who Punishes the Barbarians Liu Zao, and Provisionally General Who Assists the State Gao Cong and others to rescue Guoyang, all under Wang Su's command.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen sent General of Pacifying the Distant Fu Yong, General Who Punishes the Barbarians Liu Zao, and Provisionally General Who Assists the State Gao Cong and others to rescue Guoyang, all under Wang Su's command.

sentences.zh: 叔業進擊，大破之，聰奔懸瓠，永收散卒徐還。

translations.literal: Shuye advanced to attack and routed them greatly; Cong fled to Xuanhu and Yong gathered the scattered troops and withdrew slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye advanced to attack and routed them greatly; Cong fled to Xuanhu and Yong gathered the scattered troops and withdrew slowly.

sentences.zh: 叔業再戰，凡斬首萬級，俘三千餘人，獲器械雜畜財物以千萬計。

translations.literal: Shuye fought again; in all they beheaded ten thousand, captured more than three thousand, and seized weapons, mixed livestock, and goods worth tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye fought again; in all they beheaded ten thousand, captured more than three thousand, and seized weapons, mixed livestock, and goods worth tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 魏主命鎖三將詣懸瓠。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor ordered the three generals chained and brought to Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen ordered the three generals chained and brought to Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 劉藻、高聰免死，徙平州；

translations.literal: Liu Zao and Gao Cong were spared death and exiled to Ping Province;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao and Gao Cong were spared death and exiled to Ping Province;

sentences.zh: 傅永奪官爵；

translations.literal: Fu Yong was stripped of office and rank;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yong was stripped of office and rank;

sentences.zh: 黜王肅為平南將軍。

translations.literal: Wang Su was demoted to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was demoted to General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 肅表請更遣軍救渦陽，魏主報曰：「觀卿意，必以藻等新敗，故難於更往。

translations.literal: Su memorialized requesting that another army be sent to rescue Guoyang; the Wei emperor replied, "Judging from your intent, you must think that because Zao and the others were newly defeated, it is hard to send them again.
translations.idiomatic: Su memorialized requesting that another army be sent to rescue Guoyang; Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen replied, "Judging from your intent, you must think that because Zao and the others were newly defeated, it is hard to send them again.

sentences.zh: 朕今少分兵則不足制敵，多分兵則禁旅有闕，卿審圖之。

translations.literal: If I send few troops now they are not enough to control the enemy; if I send many, the capital guard will be short—you weigh it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: If I send few troops now they are not enough to control the enemy; if I send many, the capital guard will be short—you weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 義陽當止則止，當下則下；

translations.literal: At Yiyang stop if you should stop, descend if you should descend;
translations.idiomatic: At Yiyang stop if you should stop, descend if you should descend;

sentences.zh: 若失渦陽，卿之過也。」

translations.literal: if Guoyang is lost, the fault is yours."
translations.idiomatic: if Guoyang is lost, the fault is yours."

sentences.zh: 肅乃解義陽之圍，與統軍楊大眼、奚康生等步騎十餘萬救渦陽。

translations.literal: Su then lifted the siege of Yiyang and, with Commander Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others, marched infantry and cavalry of more than a hundred thousand to rescue Guoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Su then lifted the siege of Yiyang and, with Commander Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others, marched infantry and cavalry of more than a hundred thousand to rescue Guoyang.

sentences.zh: 叔業見魏兵盛，夜，引軍退；

translations.literal: When Shuye saw the Wei army was strong, by night he drew off his army;
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye saw the Wei army was strong, by night he drew off his army;

sentences.zh: 明日，士眾奔潰，魏人追之，殺傷不可勝數。

translations.literal: the next day the troops fled in rout; the Wei men pursued and killed and wounded beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: the next day the troops fled in rout; the Wei forces pursued and killed and wounded beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 叔業還保渦口。

translations.literal: Shuye withdrew to hold the mouth of the Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye withdrew to hold the mouth of the Guo.

sentences.zh: 初，魏中尉李彪，家世孤微，朝無親援；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Chief of the Imperial Guards Li Biao came from a poor and humble family line with no kin support at court;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Chief of the Imperial Guards Li Biao came from a poor and humble family line with no kin support at court;

sentences.zh: 初游代都，以清淵文穆公李沖好士，傾心附之。

translations.literal: on his first travels in the capital of Dai he found that Duke of Qingyuan, the Cultured and Martial Lord Li Chong, loved scholars, and he devoted himself to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: on his first travels in the capital of Dai he found that Duke of Qingyuan, the Cultured and Martial Lord Li Chong, loved scholars, and he devoted himself to Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖亦重其材學，禮遇甚厚，薦於魏主，且為之延譽於朝，公私汲引。

translations.literal: Chong also valued his talent and learning, treated him with great courtesy, recommended him to the Wei emperor, and praised him in court; in public and private he drew him upward.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also valued his talent and learning, treated him with great courtesy, recommended him to Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen, and praised him in court; in public and private he drew him upward.

sentences.zh: 及為中尉，彈劾不避貴戚，魏主賢之，以比汲黯。

translations.literal: When he became Chief of the Imperial Guards, he impeached without avoiding the noble and kin; the Wei emperor esteemed him and compared him to Ji An.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Chief of the Imperial Guards, he impeached without avoiding the noble and kin; Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen esteemed him and compared him to Ji An.

sentences.zh: 彪自以結知人主，不復藉沖，稍稍疏之，唯公坐斂袂而已，無復宗敬這意，沖浸銜之。

translations.literal: Biao considered himself bound to the sovereign's favor and no longer relied on Chong; he gradually kept his distance, and at formal audiences merely drew in his sleeves—no longer showing the deference of former days—and Chong came to resent him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, believing he had won the emperor's personal regard, no longer leaned on Chong; he grew gradually distant, and at court merely folded his sleeves at formal audience without the respect he had once shown. Chong nursed a growing grudge.

sentences.zh: 及魏主南伐，彪與沖及任城王澄共掌留務。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor marched south, Biao, Chong, and Prince of Rencheng Cheng jointly managed affairs left at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen marched south, Biao, Chong, and Prince of Rencheng Cheng jointly managed affairs at the rear capital.

sentences.zh: 彪性剛豪，意議多所乖異，數與沖爭辨，形於聲色；

translations.literal: Biao was by nature bold and overbearing; his views often diverged, and he repeatedly debated with Chong, showing it in voice and countenance;
translations.idiomatic: Biao was by nature bold and domineering; his views often clashed with Chong's, and they argued repeatedly, their quarrels breaking into raised voices and angry faces;

sentences.zh: 自以身為法官，它人莫能糾劾，事多專恣。

translations.literal: considering himself the judicial officer so that no one else could impeach him, and his conduct was often arbitrary and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: trusting that as chief judicial officer no one could impeach him, he acted with broad arbitrary license.

sentences.zh: 沖不勝忿，乃積其前作過惡，禁彪於尚書省，上表劾彪：「違傲高亢，公行僭逸，坐輿禁省，私取官材，輒駕乘黃，無所憚懾。

translations.literal: Chong could not contain his anger; he gathered Biao's past offenses, detained Biao in the Department of State Affairs, and submitted a memorial impeaching Biao: "Insolent, lofty, and defiant; he openly indulges in presumptuous ease, sits in a carriage within the forbidden offices of the secretariat, takes official materials for private use, and drives the imperial yellow carriage at will, without fear or restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Chong could not contain his anger; he gathered Biao's past offenses, detained Biao in the Department of State Affairs, and submitted a memorial impeaching Biao: "Insolent, lofty, and defiant; he openly indulges in presumptuous ease, sits in a carriage within the forbidden offices of the secretariat, takes official materials for private use, and drives the imperial yellow carriage at will, without fear or restraint.

sentences.zh: 臣輒集尚書已下、令史已上於尚書都座，以彪所犯罪狀告彪，訊其虛實，彪皆伏罪。

translations.literal: Your servant has assembled all officials from the Director of the Department down through the clerks at the central dais of the Secretariat, announced to Biao the crimes charged against him, examined truth and falsehood, and Biao confessed to all.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has assembled all officials from the Director of the Department down through the clerks at the central dais of the Secretariat, announced to Biao the crimes charged against him, examined truth and falsehood, and Biao confessed to all.

sentences.zh: 請以見事免彪所居職，付廷尉治罪。」

translations.literal: I request that he be removed from his present offices on the basis of these facts and handed over to the Court of Judicial Review for punishment."
translations.idiomatic: I request that he be removed from his present offices on the basis of these facts and handed over to the Court of Judicial Review for punishment."

sentences.zh: 沖又表稱：「臣與彪相識以來，垂二十載。

translations.literal: Chong submitted a further memorial stating: "From the time I came to know Biao, nearly twenty years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong submitted a further memorial stating: "From the time I came to know Biao, nearly twenty years have passed.

sentences.zh: 見其才優學博。

translations.literal: I saw that his talent was outstanding and his learning broad.
translations.idiomatic: I saw that his talent was outstanding and his learning broad.

sentences.zh: 議論剛正，愚意誠謂拔萃公清之人。

translations.literal: His discourse was firm and upright; in my humble opinion he was truly a man who stood above the common run—public-spirited and clean-handed.
translations.idiomatic: His discourse was firm and upright; in my humble opinion he was truly a man who stood above the common run—public-spirited and clean-handed.

sentences.zh: 後稍察其為人酷急，猶謂益多損少。

translations.literal: Later I came gradually to perceive that his character was harsh and precipitate, yet I still judged that the gains outweighed the losses.
translations.idiomatic: Later I came gradually to perceive that his character was harsh and precipitate, yet I still judged that the gains outweighed the losses.

sentences.zh: 自大駕南行以來，彪兼尚書，日夕共事，始知其專恣無忌，尊身忽物；

translations.literal: Since the imperial coach went south, Biao has held concurrent charge as Director; working with him day and night, I have begun to know his arbitrary willfulness without restraint, his esteem for himself and contempt for others;
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial coach went south, Biao has held concurrent charge as Director; working with him day and night, I have begun to know his arbitrary willfulness without restraint, his esteem for himself and contempt for others;

sentences.zh: 聽其言如振古忠恕之賢，校其行實天下佞暴之賊。

translations.literal: hear his words like the loyal and forgiving sages of old, yet compare his conduct and he is in truth the flatterer and tyrant of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: hear his words like the loyal and forgiving sages of old, yet compare his conduct and he is in truth the flatterer and tyrant of the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣與任城卑躬曲己，若順弟之奉暴兄，其所欲者，事雖非理，無不屈從。

translations.literal: The Prince of Rencheng and I bowed low and bent ourselves, like obedient younger brothers serving a violent elder brother; whatever he wanted, however unreasonable, we did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng and I bowed low and bent ourselves, like obedient younger brothers serving a violent elder brother; whatever he wanted, however unreasonable, we did not refuse.

sentences.zh: 依事求實，悉有成驗。

translations.literal: Seek the facts in each matter and all of this can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Seek the facts in each matter and all of this can be verified.

sentences.zh: 如臣列得實，宜殛彪於北荒，以除亂政之奸；

translations.literal: If what your servant has listed proves true, Biao should be executed in the northern wilds to remove the scoundrel who disrupts governance;
translations.idiomatic: If what your servant has listed proves true, Biao should be executed in the northern wilds to remove the scoundrel who disrupts governance;

sentences.zh: 所引無證，宜投臣於四裔，以息青蠅之譖。」

translations.literal: if what I cite lacks proof, your servant should be cast to the four borderlands to still the slander of the blueflies."
translations.idiomatic: if what I cite lacks proof, your servant should be cast to the four borderlands to still the slander of the blueflies."

sentences.zh: 沖手自作表，家人不知。

translations.literal: Chong wrote the memorial in his own hand; his household knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong wrote the memorial in his own hand; his household knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 帝覽表，歎悵久之，曰：「不意留台乃至於此！」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and sighed in distress for a long while, saying, "I never expected the rear capital to come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen read the memorial and sighed in distress for a long while, saying, "I never expected the rear capital to come to this!"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「道固可謂溢矣，而僕射亦為滿也。」

translations.literal: Then he said, "The Way may indeed be said to overflow—and the Vice Director is full as well."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "The Way may indeed be said to overflow—and the Vice Director is full as well."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宋弁素怨沖，而與彪同州相善，陰左右之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Song Bian had long resented Chong but was on good terms with Biao as a fellow townsman; in secret he influenced matters in Biao's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Song Bian had long resented Chong but was on good terms with Biao as a fellow townsman; in secret he influenced matters in Biao's favor.

sentences.zh: 有司處彪大辟，帝宥之，除名而已。

translations.literal: The relevant offices sentenced Biao to execution; the emperor pardoned him and merely struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices sentenced Biao to execution; the emperor pardoned him and merely struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 沖雅性溫厚，及收彪之際，親數彪前後過失，瞋目大呼，投折幾案，御史皆泥首面縛。

translations.literal: Chong was by nature mild and generous; yet at the seizure of Biao he himself enumerated Biao's offenses past and present, glared and shouted, smashed and broke desks, and all the censors knelt bound with faces to the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was by nature mild and generous; yet at the seizure of Biao he himself enumerated Biao's offenses past and present, glared and shouted, smashed and broke desks, and all the censors knelt bound with faces to the earth.

sentences.zh: 沖詈辱肆口，遂發病荒悸，言語錯繆，時扼腕大罵，稱「李彪小人」，醫藥皆不能療，或以為肝裂，旬餘而卒。

translations.literal: Chong poured forth abuse without restraint, then fell ill with frenzy and palpitations, his speech confused; at times he clutched his wrists and raged, calling "Li Biao, base fellow"; medicine could not cure him—some thought his liver had split—and within ten-odd days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chong poured forth abuse without restraint, then fell ill with frenzy and palpitations, his speech confused; at times he clutched his wrists and raged, calling "Li Biao, base fellow"; medicine could not cure him—some thought his liver had split—and within ten-odd days he died.

sentences.zh: 帝哭之，悲不自勝，贈司空。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him, overcome with grief, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen wept for him, overcome with grief, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 沖勤敏強力，久處要劇，文案盈積，終日視事，未嘗厭倦，職業修舉，才四十而發白。

translations.literal: Chong was diligent, quick, and strong; long in weighty posts, with documents piled high, he handled affairs all day without weariness; his duties were admirably discharged, and his hair had turned white by forty.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was diligent, quick, and strong; long in weighty posts, with documents piled high, he handled affairs all day without weariness; his duties were admirably discharged, and his hair had turned white by forty.

sentences.zh: 兄弟六人，凡四母，少時頗多忿競。

translations.literal: He had six brothers by four mothers in all, and in youth there had been much quarreling.
translations.idiomatic: He had six brothers by four mothers in all, and in youth there had been much quarreling.

sentences.zh: 及沖貴，祿賜皆與共之，更成敦睦。

translations.literal: When Chong rose to eminence he shared salary and gifts with them all, and they became again harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong rose to eminence he shared salary and gifts with them all, and they became again harmonious.

sentences.zh: 然多授引族姻，私以官爵，一家歲祿萬匹有餘，時人以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he recommended many kinsmen by marriage and bestowed offices and titles privately; one household's yearly stipend exceeded ten thousand bolts of silk, and contemporaries looked down on him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he recommended many kinsmen by marriage and bestowed offices and titles privately; one household's yearly stipend exceeded ten thousand bolts of silk, and contemporaries looked down on him for this.

sentences.zh: 魏主以彭城王勰為宗師，詔使督察宗室，有不帥教者以聞。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor made Prince of Pengcheng Xie clan tutor and ordered him to oversee the imperial clan and report those not obedient to instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen made Prince of Pengcheng Xie clan tutor and ordered him to oversee the imperial clan and report those not obedient to instruction.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲寅，改元。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiayin, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiayin, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 大司馬會稽太守王敬則，自以高、武舊將，必不自安。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal and Kuaiji governor Wang Jingze, as an old officer of the Gao and Wu emperors, knew he could not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal and Kuaiji governor Wang Jingze, as an old officer of the Gao and Wu emperors, knew he could not feel secure.

sentences.zh: 上雖外禮甚厚，而內相疑備，數訪問敬則飲食，體干堪宜。

translations.literal: The emperor outwardly treated him with great courtesy yet inwardly suspected and guarded against him, repeatedly inquiring after Jingze's food and drink and whether his body remained fit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming outwardly treated him with great courtesy yet inwardly suspected and guarded against him, repeatedly inquiring after Jingze's food and drink and whether his body remained fit.

sentences.zh: 聞其衰老，且以居內地，故得少寬。

translations.literal: Hearing that he had aged, and since he held an interior post, the emperor relaxed his wariness somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that he had aged, and since he held an interior post, Emperor Ming relaxed his wariness somewhat.

sentences.zh: 前二歲，上遣領軍將軍蕭坦之將齋仗五百人行武進陵，敬則諸子在都，憂怖無計。

translations.literal: Two years before, the emperor had sent Commander of the Guards Xiao Tanzhi with five hundred ceremonial guards to march at Wujin Mausoleum; Jingze's sons in the capital were terrified and at their wits' end.
translations.idiomatic: Two years before, Emperor Ming had sent Commander of the Guards Xiao Tanzhi with five hundred ceremonial guards to march at Wujin Mausoleum; Jingze's sons in the capital were terrified and at their wits' end.

sentences.zh: 上知之，遣敬則世子仲雄入東安尉之。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of this and sent Jingze's heir Zhongxiong into the Eastern Peace quarter to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming learned of this and sent Jingze's heir Zhongxiong into the Eastern Peace quarter to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 仲雄善琴，上以蔡邕焦尾琴借之。

translations.literal: Zhongxiong was skilled at the zither; the emperor lent him Cai Yong's "Scorched Tail" lute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiong was skilled at the zither; Emperor Ming lent him Cai Yong's "Scorched Tail" lute.

sentences.zh: 仲雄於御前鼓琴作《懊惱歌》，曰：「常歎負情儂，郎今果行許。」

translations.literal: Before the throne Zhongxiong played the zither and sang the Song of Vexation, saying, "So often I lamented a faithless love—and now, my lord, you have truly gone and done it."
translations.idiomatic: Before the throne Zhongxiong played the zither and sang the Song of Vexation, saying, "So often I lamented a faithless love—and now, my lord, you have truly gone and done it."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「君行不淨心，那得晉人題！」

translations.literal: He also said, "Your heart was never pure—how could you win verse from a Jin gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Your heart was never pure—how could you win verse from a Jin gentleman!"

sentences.zh: 上愈猜愧。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more suspicious and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming grew still more suspicious and ashamed.

sentences.zh: 上疾屢危，乃以光祿大夫張瑰為平東將軍、吳郡太守，置兵佐以密防敬則。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness repeatedly turned critical; he therefore made Palace Counselor Zhang Gui General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Wu commandery, with military aides to guard Jingze in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's illness repeatedly turned critical; he therefore made Palace Counselor Zhang Gui General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Wu commandery, with military aides to guard Jingze in secret.

sentences.zh: 中外傳言，當有異處分。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court it was rumored that unusual measures were coming.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court it was rumored that unusual measures were coming.

sentences.zh: 敬則聞之，竊曰：「東今有誰，只是鵒平我耳；

translations.literal: Jingze heard this and said privately, "Who is there now in the east? Only Tanzhi has been sent to pacify me;
translations.idiomatic: Jingze heard this and said privately, "Who is there now in the east? Only Tanzhi has been sent to pacify me;

sentences.zh: 東亦何易可平！

translations.literal: and the east is not so easily pacified!
translations.idiomatic: and the east is not so easily pacified!

sentences.zh: 吾終不受金罌！」

translations.literal: I will never accept the poisoned cup!"
translations.idiomatic: I will never accept the poisoned cup!"

sentences.zh: 金罌，謂鴆也。

translations.literal: "Golden goblet" means poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: "Golden goblet" means poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 敬則女為徐州行事謝朓妻，敬則子太子洗馬幼隆遣正員將軍徐岳以情告朓：「為計若同者，當往報敬則。」

translations.literal: Jingze's daughter was wife to Xie Tiao, acting prefect of Xu Province; Jingze's son Youlong, Groom of the Heir Apparent, sent Regular General Xu Yue to confide in Tiao: "If your plans agree with ours, you should go inform Jingze."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's daughter was wife to Xie Tiao, acting prefect of Xu Province; Jingze's son Youlong, Groom of the Heir Apparent, sent Regular General Xu Yue to confide in Tiao: "If your plans agree with ours, you should go inform Jingze."

sentences.zh: 朓執岳，馳啟以聞。

translations.literal: Tiao seized Yue and galloped off with a memorial to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao seized Yue and galloped off with a memorial to report it.

sentences.zh: 敬則城局參軍徐庶，家在京口。

translations.literal: Jingze's clerk Xu Shu had his family at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's clerk Xu Shu had his family at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 其子密以報庶，庶以告敬則五官掾王公林。

translations.literal: His son secretly reported to Shu, and Shu told Jingze's Registrar Wang Gonglin.
translations.idiomatic: His son secretly reported to Shu, and Shu told Jingze's Registrar Wang Gonglin.

sentences.zh: 公林，敬則族子也，常所委信。

translations.literal: Gonglin was Jingze's clansman, whom he habitually trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Gonglin was Jingze's clansman, whom he habitually trusted.

sentences.zh: 公林勸敬則急送啟賜兒死，單舟星夜還都。

translations.literal: Gonglin urged Jingze urgently to send a memorial begging that his sons be granted death, and return to the capital alone by boat through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Gonglin urged Jingze urgently to send a memorial begging that his sons be granted death, and return to the capital alone by boat through the night.

sentences.zh: 敬則令司馬張思祖草啟，既而曰：「若爾，諸郎在都，要應有信，且忍一夕。」

translations.literal: Jingze had his Marshal Zhang Sizu draft the memorial, then said, "If it were so, my sons in the capital ought surely to have sent word—let us wait one night."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze had his Marshal Zhang Sizu draft the memorial, then said, "If it were so, my sons in the capital ought surely to have sent word—let us wait one night."

sentences.zh: 其夜，呼僚佐文武樗蒲，謂眾曰：「卿諸人欲令我作何計？」

translations.literal: That night he summoned his civil and military staff to play liubo and said to the assembly, "What course do you gentlemen wish me to take?"
translations.idiomatic: That night he summoned his civil and military staff to play liubo and said to the assembly, "What course do you gentlemen wish me to take?"

sentences.zh: 莫敢先答。

translations.literal: No one dared answer first.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared answer first.

sentences.zh: 防閣丁興懷曰：「官祗應作爾！」

translations.literal: Gate guard Ding Xinghuai said, "My lord can only do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Gate guard Ding Xinghuai said, "My lord can only do this!"

sentences.zh: 敬則不應。

translations.literal: Jingze did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze did not reply.

sentences.zh: 明旦，召山陰令王詢、台傳御史鐘離祖願，敬則橫刀跂坐，問詢等：「發丁可得幾人？

translations.literal: At dawn he summoned Shanyin magistrate Wang Xun and investigating censor Zhongli Zuyuan; Jingze sat astride his seat with sword across his knees and asked Xun and the others, "How many men can be levied?
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he summoned Shanyin magistrate Wang Xun and investigating censor Zhongli Zuyuan; Jingze sat astride his seat with sword across his knees and asked Xun and the others, "How many men can be levied?

sentences.zh: 庫見有幾錢物？」

translations.literal: How much money and goods are in the treasury?"
translations.idiomatic: How much money and goods are in the treasury?"

sentences.zh: 詢稱「縣丁猝不可集」；

translations.literal: Xun said, "The county levies cannot suddenly be assembled";
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "The county levies cannot suddenly be assembled";

sentences.zh: 祖願稱「庫物多未輸入」。

translations.literal: Zuyuan said, "Much in the treasury has not yet been delivered in."
translations.idiomatic: Zuyuan said, "Much in the treasury has not yet been delivered in."

sentences.zh: 敬則怒，將出斬之，王公林又諫曰：「凡事皆可悔，唯此事不可悔；

translations.literal: Jingze grew angry and was about to have them taken out and beheaded; Wang Gonglin again remonstrated, saying, "Everything can be regretted—only this cannot be regretted;
translations.idiomatic: Jingze grew angry and was about to have them taken out and beheaded; Wang Gonglin again remonstrated, saying, "Everything can be regretted—only this cannot be regretted;

sentences.zh: 官詎不更思！」

translations.literal: will my lord not reconsider!"
translations.idiomatic: will my lord not reconsider!"

sentences.zh: 敬則唾其面曰：「我作事，何關汝小子！」

translations.literal: Jingze spat in his face and said, "What I do is none of your business, boy!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingze spat in his face and said, "What I do is none of your business, boy!"

sentences.zh: 丁卯，敬則舉兵反，招集，配衣，二三日便發。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Jingze raised troops in rebellion, mustered men, issued military garb, and set out within two or three days.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Jingze raised troops in rebellion, mustered men, issued military garb, and set out within two or three days.

sentences.zh: 前中書令何胤，棄官隱居若邪山，敬則欲劫以為尚書令。

translations.literal: Former Director of the Secretariat He Yin had abandoned office and lived in seclusion on Mount Ruoye; Jingze wished to seize him and make him Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Former Director of the Secretariat He Yin had abandoned office and lived in seclusion on Mount Ruoye; Jingze wished to seize him and make him Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 長史王弄璋等諫曰：「何令高蹈，必不從；

translations.literal: Chief of Staff Wang Nongzhang and others remonstrated, saying, "Director He walks the high path and will surely not comply;
translations.idiomatic: Chief of Staff Wang Nongzhang and others remonstrated, saying, "Director He walks the high path and will surely not comply;

sentences.zh: 不從，便應殺之。

translations.literal: if he does not comply, he should be killed.
translations.idiomatic: if he does not comply, he should be killed.

sentences.zh: 舉大事先殺名賢，事必不濟。」

translations.literal: To launch a great undertaking by first killing a famed worthy—the affair will surely not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: To launch a great undertaking by first killing a famed worthy—the affair will surely not succeed."

sentences.zh: 敬則乃止。

translations.literal: Jingze thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 胤，尚之之孫也。

translations.literal: Yin was grandson of He Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was grandson of He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏發州郡兵二十萬人，期八月中旬集懸瓠。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Wei mobilized two hundred thousand troops from the provinces and commanderies, with a deadline of mid-eighth month to assemble at Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Northern Wei mobilized two hundred thousand troops from the provinces and commanderies, with a deadline of mid-eighth month to assemble at Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 魏趙郡靈王幹卒。

translations.literal: Wei Prince Ling of Zhao commandery Gan died.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Prince Ling of Zhao commandery Gan died.

sentences.zh: 上聞王敬則反，收王幼隆及其兄員外郎世雄、記室參軍季哲、其弟太子舍人少安等，皆殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Wang Jingze had rebelled; he arrested Wang Youlong and his elder brother Staff Officer Shixiong, Recorder of the Heir Apparent Jizhe, and his younger brother Palace Attendant Shao'an, and had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming heard that Wang Jingze had rebelled; he arrested Wang Youlong and his elder brother Staff Officer Shixiong, Recorder of the Heir Apparent Jizhe, and his younger brother Palace Attendant Shao'an, and had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 長子黃門郎元遷將千人在徐州擊魏，敕徐州刺史徐玄慶殺之。

translations.literal: His eldest son, Palace Attendant Yuanyuan, was leading a thousand men at Xu Province to attack Wei; an edict ordered Xu regional inspector Xu Xuanqing to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Palace Attendant Yuanyuan, was leading a thousand men at Xu Province to attack Northern Wei; an edict ordered Xu regional inspector Xu Xuanqing to kill him.

sentences.zh: 前吳郡太守南康候子恪，嶷之子也，敬則起兵，以奉子恪為名；

translations.literal: Former Wu governor Marquis of Nankang Zike, son of Xiao Yan, had raised troops in Jingze's name to support Zike;
translations.idiomatic: Former Wu governor Marquis of Nankang Zike, son of Xiao Yan, had raised troops in Jingze's name to support Zike;

sentences.zh: 子恪亡走，未知所在。

translations.literal: Zike had fled and his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zike had fled and his whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光勸上盡誅高、武子孫，於是悉召諸王侯入宮。

translations.literal: Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang urged the emperor to execute all descendants of the Gao and Wu emperors; thereupon all princes and marquises were summoned into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang urged Emperor Ming to execute all descendants of the Gao and Wu emperors; thereupon all princes and marquises were summoned into the palace.

sentences.zh: 晉安王寶義江陵公寶覽等處中書省，高、武諸孫處西省，敕人各從左右兩人，過此依軍法；

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an Baoyi, Duke of Jiangling Baolan, and others were placed in the Secretariat; the Gao and Wu grandsons were placed in the Western Offices; an order allowed each man only two attendants at left and right—more than that would be punished by military law;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin'an Baoyi, Duke of Jiangling Baolan, and others were placed in the Secretariat; the Gao and Wu grandsons were placed in the Western Offices; an order allowed each man only two attendants at left and right—more than that would be punished by military law;

sentences.zh: 孩幼者與乳母俱入。

translations.literal: infants entered together with their wet nurses.
translations.idiomatic: infants entered together with their wet nurses.

sentences.zh: 其夜，令太醫煮椒二斛，都水辦棺材數十具，須三更，當盡殺之。

translations.literal: That night the emperor ordered the court physicians to boil two hu of pepper, the Directorate of Waterworks to prepare several dozen coffins, and at the third watch all were to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Emperor Ming ordered the court physicians to boil two hu of pepper, the Directorate of Waterworks to prepare several dozen coffins, and at the third watch all were to be killed.

sentences.zh: 子恪徒跣自歸，二更達建陽門，剌啟。

translations.literal: Zike came back barefoot; at the second watch he reached the Jianyang Gate and submitted an urgent memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zike came back barefoot; at the second watch he reached the Jianyang Gate and submitted an urgent memorial.

sentences.zh: 時刻已至，而上眠不起，中書舍人沈徽孚與上所親左右單景雋共謀少留其事。

translations.literal: The hour had come, yet the emperor slept and would not rise; Palace Secretary Shen Huifu and the emperor's close attendant Shan Jingjun together plotted to delay the matter a little.
translations.idiomatic: The hour had come, yet Emperor Ming slept and would not rise; Palace Secretary Shen Huifu and the emperor's close attendant Shan Jingjun together plotted to delay the matter a little.

sentences.zh: 須臾，上覺，景雋啟子恪已至。

translations.literal: After a moment the emperor awoke; Jingjun reported that Zike had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After a moment Emperor Ming awoke; Jingjun reported that Zike had arrived.

sentences.zh: 上驚問曰：「未邪？

translations.literal: The emperor asked in alarm, "Not yet?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming asked in alarm, "Not yet?

sentences.zh: 未邪？」

translations.literal: Not yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Not yet?"

sentences.zh: 景雋具以事對。

translations.literal: Jingjun reported the whole affair in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun reported the whole affair in detail.

sentences.zh: 上撫床曰：「遙光幾誤人事！」

translations.literal: The emperor struck the bed and said, "Yaoguang nearly ruined everything!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming struck the bed and said, "Yaoguang nearly ruined everything!"

sentences.zh: 乃賜王侯供饌，明日，悉遣還第。

translations.literal: He then granted the princes and marquises provisions; the next day he sent them all back to their residences.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted the princes and marquises provisions; the next day he sent them all back to their residences.

sentences.zh: 以子恪為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He appointed Zike Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zike Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 寶覽，緬之子也。

translations.literal: Baolan was son of Xiao Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Baolan was son of Xiao Mian.

sentences.zh: 敬則帥實甲萬人過浙江。

translations.literal: Jingze led ten thousand men in real armor across the Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze led ten thousand men in real armor across the Zhe River.

sentences.zh: 張瑰遣兵三千拒敬則於松江，聞敬則軍鼓聲，一時散走，瑰棄郡，逃民間。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui sent three thousand troops to oppose Jingze at Song River; hearing the drums of Jingze's army, they scattered at once; Gui abandoned the commandery and fled among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui sent three thousand troops to oppose Jingze at Song River; hearing the drums of Jingze's army, they scattered at once; Gui abandoned the commandery and fled among the people.

sentences.zh: 敬則以舊將舉事，百姓擔篙荷鍤，隨之者十餘萬眾；

translations.literal: Jingze raised the standard as a veteran general; common people shouldered poles and carried spades, and more than a hundred thousand followed;
translations.idiomatic: Jingze raised the standard as a veteran general; common people shouldered poles and carried spades, and more than a hundred thousand followed;

sentences.zh: 至晉陵，南沙人范修化殺縣令公上延孫以應之。

translations.literal: reaching Jinling, Fan Xiuhua of Nansha killed magistrate Gongshang Yansun to join him.
translations.idiomatic: reaching Jinling, Fan Xiuhua of Nansha killed magistrate Gongshang Yansun to join him.

sentences.zh: 敬則至武進陵口，慟哭而過。

translations.literal: Jingze came to the mouth of Wujin Mausoleum and passed through wailing in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze came to the mouth of Wujin Mausoleum and passed through wailing in grief.

sentences.zh: 烏程丘仲孚為曲阿令，敬則前鋒奄至，仲孚謂吏民曰：「賊乘勝雖銳，而烏合易離。

translations.literal: Qiu Zhongfu of Wucheng was magistrate of Qu'e; Jingze's vanguard suddenly arrived, and Zhongfu said to officials and people, "The rebels are sharp in victory, but a mob easily scatters.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongfu of Wucheng was magistrate of Qu'e; Jingze's vanguard suddenly arrived, and Zhongfu said to officials and people, "The rebels are sharp in victory, but a mob easily scatters.

sentences.zh: 今若收船艦，鑿長岡埭，瀉瀆水以阻其路，得留數日，台軍必至，如此，則大事濟矣。」

translations.literal: If we now gather boats and ships, cut the Long Hill dam, and drain the channel water to block their route, we can hold them several days; the capital army will surely come—thus the great affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If we now gather boats and ships, cut the Long Hill dam, and drain the channel water to block their route, we can hold them several days; the capital army will surely come—thus the great affair will succeed."

sentences.zh: 敬則軍至，值瀆涸，果頓兵不得進。

translations.literal: When Jingze's army arrived, the channel happened to be dry; indeed his troops halted and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingze's army arrived, the channel happened to be dry; indeed his troops halted and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，詔前軍司馬左興盛、後軍將軍崔恭祖、輔國將軍劉山陽、龍驤將軍、馬軍主胡松築壘於曲阿長岡；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renwu, an edict ordered former army marshal Zuo Xingsheng, rear army general Cui Gongzu, aide to the army general Liu Shanyang, and Dragon-Charger General and cavalry commander Hu Song to build fortifications at Long Hill in Qu'e;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu, an edict ordered former army marshal Zuo Xingsheng, rear army general Cui Gongzu, aide to the army general Liu Shanyang, and Dragon-Charger General and cavalry commander Hu Song to build fortifications at Long Hill in Qu'e;

sentences.zh: 右僕射沈文季為持節都督，屯湖頭，備京口路。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Shen Wenji was made commissioner with the tally of authority, encamped at Hutou, and guarded the Jingkou route.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Shen Wenji was made commissioner with the tally of authority, encamped at Hutou, and guarded the Jingkou route.

sentences.zh: 恭祖，慧景之旅也。

translations.literal: Gongzu had been a subordinate of Huijing.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu had been a subordinate of Huijing.

sentences.zh: 敬則急攻興盛、山陽二壘，台軍不能敵，欲退，而圍不開，各死戰。

translations.literal: Jingze pressed the attack on the two forts of Xingsheng and Shanyang; the capital army could not withstand him and wished to withdraw, but the encirclement would not open, and each side fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze pressed the attack on the two forts of Xingsheng and Shanyang; the capital army could not withstand him and wished to withdraw, but the encirclement would not open, and each side fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 胡松引騎兵突其後，白丁無器仗，皆驚散。

translations.literal: Hu Song led cavalry in a thrust at their rear; the common levies without arms and gear all scattered in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song led cavalry in a thrust at their rear; the common levies without arms and gear all scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 敬則軍大敗，索馬再上，不能得，崔恭祖刺之仆地，興盛軍客袁文曠斬之。

translations.literal: Jingze's army was utterly defeated; he sought a horse to mount again but could not find one; Cui Gongzu stabbed him so he fell to the ground, and Xingsheng's staff adviser Yuan Wenkuan beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's army was utterly defeated; he sought a horse to mount again but could not find one; Cui Gongzu stabbed him so he fell to the ground, and Xingsheng's staff adviser Yuan Wenkuan beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，傳首建康。

translations.literal: On yiyou, his head was sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, his head was sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 是時上疾已篤，敬則倉猝東起，朝廷震懼。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor's illness was already grave; Jingze had risen hastily in the east, and the court was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor Ming's illness was already grave; Jingze had risen hastily in the east, and the court was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 太子寶卷使人上屋，望見征虜亭失火，謂敬則至，急裝欲走。

translations.literal: The crown prince Baojuan sent a man onto the roof; seeing fire at the Pacify-the-Barbarians Pavilion, he thought Jingze had arrived and hurriedly packed to flee.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Baojuan sent a man onto the roof; seeing fire at the Pacify-the-Barbarians Pavilion, he thought Jingze had arrived and hurriedly packed to flee.

sentences.zh: 敬則聞之，喜曰：「檀公三十六策，走為上策，計汝父子唯有走耳！」

translations.literal: Jingze heard of it and said in delight, "Lord Tan's thirty-six stratagems—flight is the best; I reckon you father and son have nothing but flight!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingze heard of it and said in delight, "Lord Tan's thirty-six stratagems—flight is the best; I reckon you father and son have nothing but flight!"

sentences.zh: 蓋時人譏檀道濟避魏之語也。

translations.literal: This was the saying of the time mocking Tan Daoji for avoiding Wei.
translations.idiomatic: This was the saying of the time mocking Tan Daoji for avoiding Wei.

sentences.zh: 敬則之來，聲勢甚盛，裁少日而敗。

translations.literal: Jingze's coming had been very imposing in sound and force, yet within only a few days he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's coming had been very imposing in sound and force, yet within only a few days he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 台軍討賊黨，晉陵民以附敬則應死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The capital army punished the rebel faction; among the people of Jinling many who had joined Jingze deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: The capital army punished the rebel faction; among the people of Jinling many who had joined Jingze deserved death.

sentences.zh: 太守王瞻上言：「愚民易動，不足窮法。」

translations.literal: Governor Wang Zhan submitted, saying, "The foolish common people are easily stirred; it is not worth pursuing the law to the limit."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Zhan submitted, saying, "The foolish common people are easily stirred; it is not worth pursuing the law to the limit."

sentences.zh: 上許之，所全活以萬數。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; those spared numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming approved; those spared numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 瞻，弘之從孫也。

translations.literal: Zhan was a great-grandnephew of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was a great-grandnephew of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 上賞謝朓之功，遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: The emperor rewarded Xie Tiao's merit and promoted him to Director of the Department of Personnel in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming rewarded Xie Tiao's merit and promoted him to Director of the Department of Personnel in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朓上表三讓，上不許。

translations.literal: Tiao submitted a memorial declining three times; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao submitted a memorial declining three times; the emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 中書疑朓官未及讓，國子祭酒沈約曰：「近世小官不讓，遂成恆俗。

translations.literal: The Secretariat doubted whether Tiao's office was high enough to warrant declining; Director of the National University Shen Yue said, "In recent times minor offices do not decline, and this has become a constant custom.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat doubted whether Tiao's office was high enough to warrant declining; Director of the National University Shen Yue said, "In recent times minor offices do not decline, and this has become a constant custom.

sentences.zh: 謝吏部今授超階，讓別有意。

translations.literal: Director Xie has now been granted a leap in rank; his declining has a separate meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Director Xie has now been granted a leap in rank; his declining has a separate meaning.

sentences.zh: 夫讓出人情，豈關官之大小邪！」

translations.literal: Declining springs from human feeling—what has it to do with the size of the office!"
translations.idiomatic: Declining springs from human feeling—what has it to do with the size of the office!"

sentences.zh: 朓妻常懷刃欲殺朓，朓不敢相見。

translations.literal: Tiao's wife often carried a blade intending to kill Tiao; Tiao did not dare meet her.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao's wife often carried a blade intending to kill Tiao; Tiao did not dare meet her.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏彭城王勰表以一歲國秩、職俸、親恤裨軍國之用。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei Prince of Pengcheng Xie memorialized offering one year's state stipend, salary, and kin-relief funds to aid military and state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Northern Wei Prince of Pengcheng Xie memorialized offering one year's state stipend, salary, and kin-relief funds to aid military and state expenses.

sentences.zh: 魏主詔曰：「割身存國，理為遠矣。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor issued an edict, "To cut the body to preserve the state—the principle is remote indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict, "To cut the body to preserve the state—the principle is remote indeed.

sentences.zh: 職俸便停，親、國聽三分受一。」

translations.literal: Salary is forthwith halted; for kin-relief and state stipend, accept one-third of each."
translations.idiomatic: Salary is forthwith halted; for kin-relief and state stipend, accept one-third of each."

sentences.zh: 壬午，又詔損皇后私府之半，六宮嬪御、五服男女供恤亦減半，在軍者三分省一，以給軍賞。

translations.literal: On renwu, another edict reduced the empress's private treasury by half, halved the provisions for the six palaces' consorts and for men and women of the five degrees of mourning, and cut by one-third those in the army, to supply military rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, another edict reduced the empress's private treasury by half, halved the provisions for the six palaces' consorts and for men and women of the five degrees of mourning, and cut by one-third those in the army, to supply military rewards.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以太子中庶子蕭衍為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On guimao, Xiao Yan, Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent, was made regional inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Xiao Yan, Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent, was made regional inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 己酉，上殂於正福殿。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the emperor died in the Zhengfu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Emperor Ming died in the Zhengfu Hall.

sentences.zh: 遺詔：「徐令可重申前命。

translations.literal: His testamentary edict said: "Director Xu may again affirm the previous appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His testamentary edict said: "Director Xu may again affirm the previous appointment.

sentences.zh: 沈文季可左僕射，江祏可右僕射，江祀可侍中，劉暄可衛尉。

translations.literal: Shen Wenji may be Left Vice Director, Jiang Shi Right Vice Director, Jiang Si Palace Attendant, Liu Xuan Commander of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenji may be Left Vice Director, Jiang Shi Right Vice Director, Jiang Si Palace Attendant, Liu Xuan Commander of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 軍政可委陳太尉；

translations.literal: Military affairs may be entrusted to Grand Marshal Chen;
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs may be entrusted to Grand Marshal Chen;

sentences.zh: 內外眾事，無大小委徐孝嗣、遙光、坦之、江祏，其大事與沈文季、江祀、劉暄參懷。

translations.literal: all affairs within and without, great and small, are entrusted to Xu Xiaosi, Yaoguang, Tanzhi, and Jiang Shi; on great matters consult with Shen Wenji, Jiang Si, and Liu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: all affairs within and without, great and small, are entrusted to Xu Xiaosi, Yaoguang, Tanzhi, and Jiang Shi; on great matters consult with Shen Wenji, Jiang Si, and Liu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 心膂之任可委劉悛、蕭惠休、崔慧景。」

translations.literal: Tasks of the heart and backbone may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Huixiu, and Cui Huijing."
translations.idiomatic: Tasks of the heart and backbone may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Huixiu, and Cui Huijing."

sentences.zh: 上性猜多慮，簡於出入，竟不郊天。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature suspicious and full of cares, sparing in going out, and never performed suburban sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was by nature suspicious and full of cares, sparing in going out, and never performed suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又深信巫覡，每出先占利害。

translations.literal: He also deeply trusted shamans and diviners; before each outing he first divined benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: He also deeply trusted shamans and diviners; before each outing he first divined benefit and harm.

sentences.zh: 東出雲西，南出雲北。

translations.literal: Going east, clouds were in the west; going south, clouds were in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Going east, clouds were in the west; going south, clouds were in the north.

sentences.zh: 初有疾，甚秘之，聽覽不輟。

translations.literal: When illness first came he kept it very secret and did not cease attending to documents.
translations.idiomatic: When illness first came he kept it very secret and did not cease attending to documents.

sentences.zh: 久之，敕台省文簿中求白魚以為藥，外始知之。

translations.literal: After a long while he ordered the secretariat and departments to search the records for white fish for medicine, and only then did the outside learn of it.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he ordered the secretariat and departments to search the records for white fish for medicine, and only then did the outside learn of it.

sentences.zh: 太子即位。

translations.literal: The crown prince ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛亥，魏太子自洛陽朝於懸瓠。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinhai, the Wei crown prince came from Luoyang to attend court at Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai, the Northern Wei crown prince came from Luoyang to attend court at Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 壬子，奉朝請鄧學以齊興郡降魏。

translations.literal: On renzi, Court Gentleman Deng Xue surrendered Qi-Xing commandery to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Court Gentleman Deng Xue surrendered Qi-Xing commandery to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主之入寇也，遣使發高車兵。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor invaded, he sent envoys to mobilize Gaoche troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen invaded, he sent envoys to mobilize Gaoche troops.

sentences.zh: 高車憚遠役，奉袁紇樹者為主，相帥北叛。

translations.literal: The Gaoche feared distant service; they made Yuan Hei Shuzhe their leader and led one another in rebellion to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche feared distant service; they made Yuan Hei Shuzhe their leader and led one another in rebellion to the north.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣征北將軍宇文福討之，大敗而還，福坐黜官。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Campaign-North General Yuwen Fu to punish them; Fu was greatly defeated and returned, and Fu was demoted and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen sent Campaign-North General Yuwen Fu to punish them; Fu was greatly defeated and returned, and Fu was demoted and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 更命平北將軍江陽王繼都督北討諸軍事以討之，自懷朔以東悉稟節度，仍攝鎮平城。

translations.literal: He then appointed Pacify-North General Prince of Jiangyang Ji to command all northern punitive military affairs; from Huaishuo east all were placed under his authority, and he still held charge of garrisoning Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Pacify-North General Prince of Jiangyang Ji to command all northern punitive military affairs; from Huaishuo east all were placed under his authority, and he still held charge of garrisoning Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 繼，熙之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Ji was a great-grandson of Xi Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was a great-grandson of Xi Zhi.

sentences.zh: 八月，葬明皇帝於興安陵，廟號高宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Emperor Ming was buried at Xing'an Mausoleum; his temple name was Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Emperor Ming was buried at Xing'an Mausoleum; his temple name was Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯惡靈在太極殿，欲速葬。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun hated the coffin in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and wished to bury it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun hated the coffin in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and wished to bury it quickly.

sentences.zh: 徐孝嗣固爭，得逾月。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosi firmly remonstrated and gained a delay of more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi firmly remonstrated and gained a delay of more than a month.

sentences.zh: 帝每當哭，輒雲喉痛。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor was to mourn, he would claim a sore throat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor was to mourn, he would claim a sore throat.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫羊闡入臨，無發，號慟俯仰，幘遂脫地。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Palace Yang Chan came to attend the lying-in-state; he was bald; wailing and bowing up and down, his cap fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Palace Yang Chan came to attend the lying-in-state; he was bald; wailing and bowing up and down, his cap fell to the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝輟哭大笑，謂左右曰：「禿鶖啼來乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor stopped mourning and laughed loudly, saying to those beside him, "Has the bald egret come crying!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stopped mourning and laughed loudly, saying to those beside him, "Has the bald egret come crying!"

sentences.zh: 九月，己亥，魏主聞高宗殂，下詔稱「禮不伐喪」，引兵還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jihai, the Wei emperor heard that Gaozong had died and issued an edict citing "ritual does not attack during mourning" and withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jihai, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen heard that Gaozong had died and issued an edict citing "ritual does not attack during mourning" and withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔北伐高車。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict ordered a northern campaign against the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, an edict ordered a northern campaign against the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 魏主得疾甚篤，旬日不見侍臣，左右唯彭城王勰等數人而已。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor's illness grew very grave; for ten days he did not see attending ministers—only Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others were at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen's illness grew very grave; for ten days he did not see attending ministers—only Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others were at his side.

sentences.zh: 勰內侍醫藥，外總軍國之務，遠近肅然，人無異議。

translations.literal: Within, Xie attended to medicine; without, he oversaw military and state affairs; near and far were solemn, and no one voiced dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Within, Xie attended to medicine; without, he oversaw military and state affairs; near and far were solemn, and no one voiced dissent.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍丹陽徐謇善醫，時在洛陽，急召之。

translations.literal: Right Army General Xu Qian of Danyang was skilled in medicine and was then at Luoyang; he was urgently summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Right Army General Xu Qian of Danyang was skilled in medicine and was then at Luoyang; he was urgently summoned.

sentences.zh: 既至，勰涕泣執手謂曰：「君能已至尊之疾，當獲意外之賞；

translations.literal: When he arrived, Xie wept, took his hand, and said, "If you can cure the Supreme One's illness, you will receive an unexpected reward;
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Xie wept, took his hand, and said, "If you can cure the Supreme One's illness, you will receive an unexpected reward;

sentences.zh: 不然，有不測之誅。

translations.literal: otherwise there is execution beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise there is execution beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 非但榮辱，乃系存亡。」

translations.literal: It is not merely honor and disgrace—it concerns survival itself."
translations.idiomatic: It is not merely honor and disgrace—it concerns survival itself."

sentences.zh: 勰又密為壇於汝水之濱，依周公故事，告天地及顯祖，乞以身代魏主。

translations.literal: Xie also secretly built an altar on the bank of the Ru River, following the precedent of the Duke of Zhou, and announced to Heaven and Earth and to the Manifest Ancestor, begging to substitute his own body for the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xie also secretly built an altar on the bank of the Ru River, following the precedent of the Duke of Zhou, and announced to Heaven and Earth and to the Manifest Ancestor, begging to substitute his own body for Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 魏主疾有間，丙午，發懸瓠，捨於汝濱，集百官，坐徐謇於上席，稱揚其功，除鴻臚卿，封金鄉縣伯，賜錢萬緡；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor's illness eased; on bingwu he set out from Xuancheng, halted on the Ru bank, gathered the hundred officials, seated Xu Qian in the place of honor, praised his merit, appointed him Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, enfeoffed him as Baron of Jinxiang county, and granted ten thousand strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen's illness eased; on bingwu he set out from Xuancheng, halted on the Ru bank, gathered the hundred officials, seated Xu Qian in the place of honor, praised his merit, appointed him Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, enfeoffed him as Baron of Jinxiang county, and granted ten thousand strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 諸王別餉賚，各不減千匹。

translations.literal: the princes each gave separate gifts, none less than a thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: the princes each gave separate gifts, none less than a thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，辛巳，魏主如鄴。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on xinsi, the Wei emperor went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on xinsi, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen went to Ye.

sentences.zh: 戊子，立妃褚氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On wuzi, he established Consort Chu as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, he established Consort Chu as empress.

sentences.zh: 魏江陽王繼上言：「高車頑昧，避役遁逃，若悉追戮，恐遂擾亂。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Jiangyang Ji submitted, saying, "The Gaoche are stubborn and dull; they flee service and escape—if all are pursued and executed, I fear disorder will follow.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Prince of Jiangyang Ji submitted, saying, "The Gaoche are stubborn and dull; they flee service and escape—if all are pursued and executed, I fear disorder will follow.

sentences.zh: 請遣使，鎮別推檢，斬魁首一人，自餘加以慰撫。

translations.literal: I request that envoys be sent to investigate separately in each garrison, execute one ringleader, and comfort and reassure the rest.
translations.idiomatic: I request that envoys be sent to investigate separately in each garrison, execute one ringleader, and comfort and reassure the rest.

sentences.zh: 若悔悟從役者，即令赴軍。」

translations.literal: Those who repent and accept service should forthwith be sent to join the army."
translations.idiomatic: Those who repent and accept service should forthwith be sent to join the army."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 於是叛者往往自歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon rebels often returned of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon rebels often returned of themselves.

sentences.zh: 繼先遣入慰諭樹者。

translations.literal: Ji first sent men in to comfort and instruct Shuzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Ji first sent men in to comfort and instruct Shuzhe.

sentences.zh: 樹者亡入柔然，尋自悔，相帥出降。

translations.literal: Shuzhe fled into Rouran; soon he repented and led his followers out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhe fled into Rouran; soon he repented and led his followers out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 魏主善之；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor approved of this;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen approved of this;

sentences.zh: 曰：「江陽可大任也。」

translations.literal: he said, "Jiangyang can bear great responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: he said, "Jiangyang can bear great responsibility."

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲寅，魏主自鄴班師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, the Wei emperor returned his army from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen returned his army from Ye.

sentences.zh: 林邑王諸農入朝，海中值風，溺死，以其子文款為林邑王。

translations.literal: King Zhunong of Linyi came to court; on the sea he met a storm and drowned; his son Wenkuan was made king of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhunong of Linyi came to court; on the sea he met a storm and drowned; his son Wenkuan was made king of Linyi.
